papers.abstract: Background and Aims: Until now, according to the EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B (CHB), the relationship between steatotic liver disease (SLD) and the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in CHB patients still yields conflicting results, with some data suggesting an increased risk of HCC, while several cohort studies have indicated a reduced risk in CHB patients with SLD. Sex is a predominant factor in the development and severity of chronic liver diseases. We aimed to understand the effect modification by sex in this association using a large population-based cohort study with long-term follow-up of patients with CHB. Approach and Results: This population-based study from Taiwan’s National Health Insurance Research Database (2009–2022) comprised two cohorts of patients with CHB aged 40–75 years: (1) 53,888 patients treated with entecavir or tenofovir, and (2) 525,109 antiviral-naive patients. HCC was identified in 4245 and 9491 patients in the treated and untreated cohorts, respectively. After adjusting for competing risk of death and relevant covariates, SLD was associated with a lower risk of HCC in males but a higher risk in females, and this sex difference (p < 0.0001 for sex–SLD interaction) was identified in both treated (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] [95% CI]: 0.85 [0.74–0.96] in males and 1.42 [1.17–1.73] in females) and untreated (0.75 [0.67–0.84] in males and 1.34 [1.14–1.56] in females) patients. Using propensity score matching with stratification by sex, further accounting for differences in medication use between SLD and non-SLD groups, yielded consistent results. The excess risk of HCC with SLD among females was mainly in those aged≥55 years, and even existed in the presence of diabetes, whereas among males, SLD exhibited an inverse association with HCC, regardless of age or diabetes. Conclusions: There was a sex disparity in the association between SLD and CHB-related HCC. Future studies and management of SLD for CHB should consider the sex disparity.

papers.abstract: Background KRAS-mutated ultra-low rectal cancer is associated with poor response to conventional neoadjuvant therapy, making sphincter preservation particularly challenging. In addition, effective rehabilitation strategies for severe low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) remain limited. Case presentation A 55-year-old woman with KRAS-mutated ultra-low rectal adenocarcinoma experienced insufficient tumor regression after multiple lines of chemotherapy, chemoradiotherapy, and immunotherapy, complicated by oxaliplatin allergy. After referral to our center, she received bevacizumab plus XELIRI combined with traditional Chinese medicine therapies. Following five treatment cycles, the patient underwent laparoscopic radical rectal resection with transanal specimen extraction and Bacon-type pull-through reconstruction. Pathological examination demonstrated negative proximal, distal, and circumferential margins, no metastatic involvement among 12 examined lymph nodes, and a final pathological stage of ypT2N0. The patient subsequently developed major LARS and underwent a four-week rehabilitation program centered on electroacupuncture at the Baliao acupoints. Assessment was conducted using the LARS score, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center Bowel Function Instrument (MSKCC-BFI), and EORTC QLQ-C30 scales. The patient’s bowel movement frequency decreased from over 30 times per day to approximately 10 times, and remained stable at 7–10 times during the 6-month follow-up. Conclusion In this patient, an individualized conversion strategy was followed by R0 sphincter-preserving resection, and postoperative bowel function improved temporally during and after multimodal rehabilitation that included electroacupuncture. This observation provide preliminary evidence in support of this treatment approach. However, high-quality studies are still required to comprehensively evaluate the efficacy of this treatment regimen.

papers.abstract: Background Nigeria bears one of the world’s largest burdens of HIV, with ongoing expansion of antiretroviral therapy (ART) significantly improving the survival of people living with HIV (PLHIV). This epidemiologic shift has changed the pattern of morbidity and mortality toward chronic conditions, especially HIV-associated malignancies (HIVAMs), including both AIDS-defining malignancies (ADMs) and non-AIDS-defining malignancies (NADMs). Despite their increasing significance, the national burden, patterns, and systemic challenges related to HIVAMs in Nigeria remain poorly understood and characterized. Methods We conducted a narrative review of peer-reviewed literature, cancer registry reports, and grey literature published between January 2000 and December 2024. Searches were carried out in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, African Journals Online, and Google Scholar, complemented by national reports from the National Agency for the Control of AIDS, the Federal Ministry of Health, and the National System of Cancer Registries. Eligible sources reported cancer occurrence among PLHIV or HIV prevalence among cancer patients in Nigeria. Findings were synthesized narratively due to significant heterogeneity across study designs and outcomes. Results Seventy-three sources met the inclusion criteria, and these were primarily hospital-based and retrospective studies. ADMs remain the most common cancers among PLHIV, notably invasive cervical cancer, Kaposi sarcoma, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with notable regional differences. Expansion of ART has been linked to a decline in Kaposi sarcoma incidence, while the burden of cervical cancer remains high, driven by persistent oncogenic HPV infection and limited screening coverage among women living with HIV (WLWH). Emerging NADMs, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, breast cancer, and ocular surface squamous neoplasia, reflect improved survival, aging, chronic immune dysregulation, and co-infections like Hepatitis B and C. Across these cancers, late-stage presentation and poor outcomes are common, largely due to fragmented HIV–cancer surveillance, inadequate pathology and radiotherapy capacity, limited molecular diagnostics, high out-of-pocket treatment costs, and weak integration of HIV and oncology services. Conclusion HIV-associated cancers pose a major yet often overlooked public health issue in Nigeria. Enhancing integrated HIV–cancer surveillance, increasing prevention and early detection efforts through ART programs, upgrading diagnostic and treatment facilities, and utilizing digital and molecular innovations are essential for decreasing preventable cancer-related morbidity and mortality among PLHIV in Nigeria.

papers.abstract: Mesothelioma mortality continues to reflect asbestos exposure because of its long latency. While previous Spanish studies focused primarily on pleural disease, this study assessed mesothelioma mortality across the ICD-10 C45 category in Spain from 1999 to 2024. A population-based time-trend study was conducted using mortality data (ICD-10 C45) from the Spanish National Statistics Institute. Age-standardised mortality rates (ASMRs) were calculated using the 2013 European Standard Population. Temporal trends and sex-specific parallelism were evaluated using Joinpoint regression. Among 9733 recorded mesothelioma deaths (7311 men, 2422 women), ASMRs were consistently higher in men, although temporal trends were parallel by sex. Overall mortality increased until 2016 (annual percentage change [APC] 2.3%, 95% CI 1.5-3.0) and subsequently declined non-significantly, yielding an average annual percentage change (AAPC) of 1.0% (95% CI 0.2-1.7) for 1999-2024. Pleural mortality increased until 2011 before declining non-significantly, whereas recorded peritoneal mortality increased throughout the study period (AAPC 2.0%, 95% CI 0.7-3.2). Deaths coded as unspecified site (C45.9) showed the largest increase in ASMR (AAPC 2.1%, 95% CI 1.1-3.1) and accounted for 43.5% of male and 31.8% of female mesothelioma deaths in 2024. Absolute mesothelioma deaths increased in Spain while age-standardised rates attenuated after 2016. The continued increase in recorded peritoneal mortality and the substantial contribution of unspecified-site deaths indicate that surveillance should not rely solely on pleural mesothelioma, highlighting the need for comprehensive monitoring of the complete ICD-10 C45 category and improved anatomical classification.

papers.abstract: The prognosis for glioblastoma (GBM) is correlated with the extent of resection. Continuous en bloc resection (CEBR) is a surgical strategy that involves the removal of the gross tumor along with its normal adjacent tissue (NAT) as "one whole block". However, its impact on the survival of patients with GBM in non-eloquent areas is unknown. We found that CEBR significantly prolongs both overall survival and progression-free survival in patients with GBM in non-eloquent areas. We further reported that the molecular drivers, transcriptomic abnormalities, and microenvironmental alterations akin to those found in tumors were detected in the NAT. These tumor-like molecular and microenvironmental alterations were predominantly present in the NAT within 10 mm around the tumor, despite the absence of identifiable tumor cells on rigorous histological examination. Overall, CEBR improved survival in patients with GBM in non-eloquent areas, while tumor-like alterations were present in brain tissue adjacent to the tumor. These findings provide the rationale to incorporate NAT into the extent of resection in the CEBR strategy and support further investigation of the association between its resection and patient prognosis.

papers.abstract: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) lacks effective targeted therapies despite frequent hyperactivation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, and the contribution of adaptor proteins to this process remains poorly defined. Here, we identify Insulin Receptor Substrate 4 (IRS4) as a common substrate of Src kinase and the phosphatase RPTPα, and uncover a previously unrecognized, conserved phosphorylation site at YY111/112 within the IRS4 PH domain. Src-mediated phosphorylation at this site is essential for IRS4-driven proliferation, anchorage-independent growth, and invasiveness in LUSC cells. Mechanistically, phosphorylation at YY111/112 induces conformational rearrangements in IRS4 that enhance the recruitment of the p85β SH2 domain to the YXXM motif of IRS4, thereby promoting AKT activation without altering IRS4 protein stability or subcellular distribution. An IRS4-derived cell-permeable phosphopeptide containing pYY111/112 disrupts the Src-IRS4 interaction and significantly suppresses tumor growth in vivo in a YY111/112-dependent manner. Consistently, YY111/112 phosphorylation is markedly elevated in human LUSC tissues and correlates with advanced disease stages. Collectively, these findings define a Src-IRS4-PI3K/AKT signaling axis and identify YY111/112 as a critical regulatory site of IRS4 and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in LUSC.

papers.abstract: Adverse drug events (ADEs) are a critical indicator of patient safety but are often documented only in free-text clinical notes. The potential of recent advances in natural language processing (NLP), particularly generative large language models (LLMs), to identify ADEs remains understudied. This study aimed to compare the performance of multiple LLMs in identifying ADE-Drug relationships in inpatient and ambulatory clinical notes. We used clinical notes from the 2018 National NLP Clinical Challenge (n2c2) ADE dataset (inpatient; n = 505) and from outpatient encounters (n = 2555) between October 1, 2018, and December 31, 2019, at a large academic medical center based in New England. Notes were pre-processed into snippets for model input. Evaluated Models included: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.2-3B and their instruction fine-tuned variants (including low-rank adapters for Llama). Performance was assessed using both strict and relaxed evaluations (precision, recall, and F1) for all models, followed by manual evaluation (exact semantic match, partial match, missing ADE, drug mention only, not a drug, or wrong) of the two best-performing models. Of the 1048 notes in the local test split, 450 (42.9%) contained at least one ADE. The n2c2 test set included 202 notes, of which 155 (76.7%) contained at least one ADE. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini were the top-performing models among those evaluated. GPT-4o consistently outperformed GPT-4o-mini in ADE extraction across both datasets, with higher F1-scores (0.524 vs. 0.381) and a more balanced precision-recall profile. Both models captured ADEs effectively in explicit and complex clinical contexts, although limitations included misclassification of pre-existing allergies and occasional conflation of therapeutic indications with adverse effects. GPT-4o achieved higher exact match coverage and fewer errors across clinical notes, indicating more reliable performance in both inpatient and ambulatory settings. This work establishes a foundation for integrating LLM methods into real-world drug safety surveillance, with direct implications for improving patient safety. None.

papers.abstract: Research over the past two decades has repositioned exercise from a general lifestyle recommendation to a potential anticancer intervention. Pooled analyses of more than 1.4 million participants link regular physical activity with lower incidence of at least 13 tumour types, and prospective cohort data report cancer-specific mortality 24-31% lower among the most active patients with breast, colorectal, prostate and lung cancer, although these estimates derive from observational designs using self-reported activity. In 2025, a phase III trial in stage III colon cancer provided the first randomised evidence that a structured exercise and behaviour-change programme improves disease-free and overall survival after adjuvant chemotherapy; a randomised trial in ovarian cancer subsequently did not show a progression-free survival benefit. Candidate mechanisms include insulin and growth-factor signalling, myokine secretion, immune mobilisation, reduced chronic inflammation and gut microbiome remodelling, although these rest on evidence ranging from cell culture to human trials and are rarely distinguished by level. Despite this evidence, structural, educational and economic barriers prevent integration of exercise into routine oncology care. This Review synthesises the available evidence and identifies the steps required for clinical adoption.

papers.abstract: Use of pegulicianine fluorescence-guided surgery (pFGS) for intraoperative residual tumor assessment in breast cancer lumpectomy surgery removed additional tumor and reduced second surgeries. This study assessed breast satisfaction among patients with and without additional margin excision and preference for optimizing cosmesis versus avoiding a second surgery. Two clinical trials randomized stages 0 to 3 breast cancer patients to pFGS or standard lumpectomy. For pFGS, additional cavity margin specimens were taken at sites of pegulicianine fluorescence after standard lumpectomy. Surveys of BREAST-Q satisfaction were administered in trials 1 and 2, and surveys of cancer worry and patient preference information (PPI) were administered in trial 2. Satisfaction surveys were completed 6 to 12 months postoperatively by 14 % of the trial 1 and 67 % of the trial 2 patients. The mean postoperative breast satisfaction score was 75.8 (n = 99; range, 15-100) for the pegulicianine-assisted arm patients versus 79.0 (n = 19; range, 35-100) for the control subjects (p = 0.53). The mean breast satisfaction score was 73.6 (n = 52; range, 33-100) among the patients with additional pFGS-assisted cavity margins taken versus 78.5 (n = 66; range, 15-100) (p = 0.17) among those with no additional tissue taken. Overall, 70.6 % of the respondents strongly preferred or preferred avoiding a second surgery, 19.6 % had no preference, and only 9.8 % preferred to optimize cosmetic outcomes. No patient strongly preferred to optimize cosmetic outcomes CONCLUSIONS: No decrease in breast satisfaction was observed among the breast cancer lumpectomy patients undergoing pFGS intraoperative margin assessment despite additional tissue removal. Most of the patients valued avoiding a second surgery over maximizing cosmetic outcome.

papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) remains a major cause of cancer mortality, yet the metabolic mechanisms that remodel metastatic RNA-splicing programs are poorly defined. Here, integrated quantitative proteomics and lysine 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation (Khib) proteomics of patient-matched normal mucosa, primary CRCs, and liver metastases revealed a progressive increase in global Khib, with enrichment on RNA-splicing proteins. Serine/arginine-rich splicing factor 9 (SRSF9) emerged as a Khib-modified splicing factor whose expression and K155 Khib levels increased from normal tissue to primary tumors and liver metastases. Gain and loss of function studies in CRC cell lines, patient-derived organoids, subcutaneous xenografts, and splenic injection liver metastasis models showed that SRSF9 promotes proliferation, invasion, tumor growth, and liver colonization. Mechanistically, K155 Khib stabilized SRSF9 protein; the K155R mutation accelerated degradation and abolished SRSF9-driven malignant phenotypes. KAT7 and SIRT6 act as regulators of Khib modification, which positively and negatively modulate the K155 Khib modification of SRSF9, respectively. SRSF9 bound CD44 pre-mRNA through its RRM1 domain and promoted alternative splicing toward the oncogenic CD44V8-10 isoform, which was elevated in patient tumors and metastases and rescued the impaired proliferation and metastatic capacity caused by SRSF9 loss. Finally, a CD44V8-10-targeting antisense oligonucleotide suppressed CRC growth and liver metastasis in preclinical models. These findings define a KAT7/SIRT6-regulated Khib-SRSF9-CD44V8-10 axis that couples metabolic acylation to metastatic splicing and nominate CD44V8-10 as a therapeutic vulnerability in CRC liver metastasis.

papers.abstract: The combination immunotherapies, including those with atezolizumab and bevacizumab (Atez/Bev), have become standard therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, its efficacy remains limited and reliable biomarkers are lacking. In this study, we analyzed paired tumor and background liver tissues from Atez/Bev-treated HCC patients and found that high programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) expression in CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) correlated with therapeutic response independent of etiology. RNA sequencing on the tumor samples revealed that the branched-chain amino acid (BCAA)-related metabolic pathway was enriched in the group with high PD-1 expression in CD8⁺ TILs. Along with in vitro experiments, we identified the importance of BCAAs for activation and differentiation of CD8+ T cells. In addition, BCAA metabolism was related to response to PD-1 blockade in not subcutaneous but intrahepatic mouse model-specific manner. Actually, public dataset analyses revealed that high expression of BCAT1, a key enzyme in BCAA metabolism, was associated with poor prognosis in HCC, but not in other cancer types. These findings suggest the importance of liver-specific BCAA metabolism in antitumor immunity and highlight the need to assess the tumor microenvironment within its organ-specific metabolic context.

papers.abstract: Placental foetal vascular malperfusion (PFVM) is a chronic disorder characterised by impaired blood flow and abnormal vascular development, inducing adverse neonatal outcomes. Long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LC-PUFAs) play a crucial role in placenta health. We aimed to explore the role of genetic variation in LC-PUFA metabolism in PFVM risk as well as underlying mechanisms. Associations were examined between two functional polymorphisms (rs174538 and rs174556) of the fatty acid desaturase 1 (FADS1) gene encoding the rate-limiting enzyme for LC-PUFA metabolism and PFVM among pregnant women (n = 646). Placental transcriptomes were correlated with PFVM and FADS1 genotypes. Various assays were performed in human umbilical vein endothelial cells and trophoblasts with FADS1 inhibitor and LC-PUFA interventions to characterise their function changes. Low-function alleles of both polymorphisms were significantly associated with increased PFVM risk and decreased placental FADS1 transcription level. In placenta tissue, lower FADS1 expression is also associated with PFVM. PFVM-associated genes are enriched to pathways related to immune responses, apoptosis, and angiogenesis, which overlap with the genes and pathways associated with the risk alleles and demonstrate a cell-type enrichment to endothelial cells. In vitro, FADS1 inhibition impairs multiple functions of and interactions between endothelial and trophoblast cells. These impairments are reversed by LC-PUFA supplementation. These findings highlight the impact of maternal LC-PUFA homoeostasis in placenta health and suggest that maternal FADS1 variants can potentially be an early diagnostic marker for PFVM. Our data supports PUFA metabolism as a precision therapeutic or preventive target to reduce placental dysfunction risk. NIH, Wayne State University and Michigan State University.

papers.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility of continuous bilateral lower-limb near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) monitoring as an adjunct to standard hourly neurovascular assessment (NVA) in patients receiving intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support, and to characterize the relationship between regional oxygen saturation (rSO₂) and in-hospital mortality. Prospective observational cohort study. Cardiac care unit of a tertiary cardiac center (Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Singapore). Fifty consecutive adult patients receiving IABP support via femoral arterial access. Continuous bilateral lower-limb rSO₂ monitoring using NIRS was performed throughout IABP support, alongside standardized hourly NVA of both limbs (capillary refill time, skin color, temperature, pulse quality, and Doppler signal). Right femoral access was used in 94% of patients (47 of 50). Minimum contralateral (left) rSO₂ was significantly lower in nonsurvivors than survivors (29.3% ± 17.6% v 43.3% ± 14.4%, p = 0.024), with a directionally similar but nonsignificant trend on the ipsilateral (right) side (p = 0.083). Regional oxygen saturation correlated moderately with capillary refill time (Spearman rank correlation [rs] ≈ 0.50) and pulse quality (rs ≈ 0.38) bilaterally but not with temperature change, which deteriorated in >92% of limbs. Low rSO₂ (<40%) in either limb was associated with a nonsignificant 3.16-fold increase in mortality odds (95% confidence interval, 0.55-18.11; p = 0.197). No patient developed acute limb ischemia. Sepsis (odds ratio [OR], 13.0) and renal replacement therapy (OR, 7.1) were the only statistically significant predictors of mortality. Continuous bilateral lower-limb rSO₂ monitoring is feasible throughout IABP support and produces a physiologically coherent signal that correlates moderately with objective NVA parameters and is lower in patients who do not survive to discharge. No limb ischemic events occurred; these findings are best regarded as feasibility and physiology data rather than evidence that continuous monitoring improves limb outcomes, and they warrant confirmation in a larger, multicenter study.

papers.abstract: To identify if the delivery of oxygen over consumption of oxygen (DO2/VO2) ratio is significantly associated with clinical outcomes such as mortality, need for heart transplantation, or need for a mechanical circulatory support device. Retrospective cohort study. Medical and surgical cardiac intensive care units of the Mayo Clinic. Adult patients (≥18 years old) admitted to the cardiothoracic surgical or cardiac intensive care units between January 2012 and December 2025 were included if they underwent invasive hemodynamic assessment with simultaneous arterial blood gas, mixed venous blood gas, hemoglobin, and mean arterial pressure. Patients were excluded if they had their venous oxygen saturations drawn from a central line or a peripherally inserted central catheter, as well as those admitted for sepsis/septic shock. No interventions were performed on patients. DO2/VO2 demonstrated a nonlinear association with mortality. Using the median value of 4.73 as a reference point, patients with a DO2/VO2 value of ∼2 had the highest likelihood of mortality. Kaplan-Meier analysis using a prespecified cut-point of 5 did not demonstrate any significant relationship with mortality, likely because of the underlying nonlinear relationship. There was no significant association between DO2/VO2 ratio and the need for mechanical circulatory support or heart transplantation. DO₂/VO₂ is a marker of systemic oxygen balance that complements conventional hemodynamic indices. A categorical threshold of 5 did not show an association with clinical outcomes, but continuous analyses did suggest that a low DO₂/VO₂ may identify a high-risk phenotype.

papers.abstract: To synthesize available evidence on perioperative management and clinical outcomes of hepatectomy in patients with Fontan circulation, focusing on hemodynamic strategies and surgical safety. A systematic review of case reports and case series. Published studies were identified through databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, ICHUSHI, and CiNii Research). Thirty-one patients from 28 studies underwent hepatectomy after the Fontan procedure. Open or laparoscopic hepatectomy, primarily for hepatocellular carcinoma in the setting of Fontan-associated liver disease. All patients had stable Fontan physiology, and no perioperative mortality was reported. Preoperative baseline central venous pressure (CVP) ranged from 10 to 15 mmHg. Intraoperative management consistently favored a baseline-CVP strategy over conventional low-CVP targets. Laparoscopic approaches uniformly used low-pressure pneumoperitoneum below baseline-CVP levels. The Pringle maneuver was well tolerated; however, inferior vena cava clamping was associated with significant hypotension. The median blood loss was 1,106 mL (range 10-4,130 mL). Congestion-related complications, including ascites, pleural effusion, heart failure, and unspecified fluid retention, were most commonly reported postoperatively. Hepatectomy appears feasible in carefully selected patients with stable Fontan circulation. Practical perioperative considerations summarized from reported patterns include maintaining CVP near baseline, minimizing increases in pulmonary vascular resistance, and keeping pneumoperitoneum pressure below baseline CVP during laparoscopic surgery. However, hepatectomy-specific risk stratification has yet to be established, and optimal perioperative management of patients with impaired Fontan physiology remains uncertain. A critical knowledge gap remains regarding hemostatic approaches that optimize bleeding control while preserving the Fontan circulation.

papers.abstract: The GID/CTLH family of E3 ubiquitin ligases employs several substrate receptor subunits that recruit distinct degrons, but the substrate recognition mechanisms of the CTLHMKLN1 assembly have largely remained elusive. Here, we reconstitute CTLHMKLN1-dependent ubiquitylation of three biochemically distinct substrates - MKLN1 itself, ZMYND19, and FAM72A-recruited UNG2, and determine cryo-EM structures of each substrate bound to MKLN1. The structures reveal how MKLN1's discoidin and Kelch β-propeller domains engage substrates through multivalent contacts. MKLN1 recruits itself through discoidin-Kelch interactions between MKLN1 dimers, forming an assembly that competes with other substrates. ZMYND19 and FAM72A each bind to MKLN1 through loops engaging the discoidin trench domain while their C-terminal Arg residues engage the MKLN1 Kelch central channel, identifying MKLN1 as an Arg/C-degron receptor. The acetylated N-terminus of UNG2 is positioned within a Y-shaped tunnel of FAM72A, defining an adaptor-mediated Ac/N-degron recognition mechanism. Thus, our data reveal how combinatorial deployment of MKLN1 discoidin and Kelch domains enable a single receptor subunit to recognize a diverse substrate repertoire, adding to a complex picture of degron recognition across the GID/CTLH family.

papers.abstract: Prehabilitation optimises patients' physical, nutritional, and psychological readiness before major surgery, but remains largely absent from Austrian clinical practice. We aimed to identify stakeholder-perceived barriers to prehabilitation implementation and assess the readiness of the healthcare system. An exploratory qualitative study using semi-structured interviews was conducted with eight purposively sampled stakeholders representing anaesthesiology (n=2), surgery (n=2), outpatient cardiology (n=1), clinical psychology (n=1), physiotherapy (n=1), and health insurance administration (n=1). Interviews conducted between February and March 2024 were analysed using descriptive thematic content analysis and mapped to the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. Six themes emerged: attitudes towards prehabilitation, work environment, healthcare system structure, economic factors, cultural factors, and politics, evidence, and guidelines. Despite unanimous recognition of clinical value, knowledge of prehabilitation varied widely. Critical barriers included the structural and financial separation between inpatient and outpatient sectors, the absence of reimbursement mechanisms, workforce shortages, organisational inertia, and limited advocacy by professional societies. Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research mapping identified barriers across all five domains, with outer setting barriers-particularly fragmented financing and the absence of national guidelines-being the most prominent. These exploratory findings reveal conceptual, systemic, and cultural barriers to prehabilitation in Austria. The simultaneous absence of integrated financing, professional society advocacy, and coordinated governance may explain Austria's particularly limited uptake compared to that in the UK and the Netherlands. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation through larger-scale qualitative studies, quantitative surveys, and pilot implementation trials that include patient perspectives and economic modelling.

papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) involves chronic inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract, which predisposes patients to an increased risk of fibrosis and cancer due to prolonged inflammatory stimulation. However, the specific mechanisms underlying secondary gastrointestinal carcinogenesis in individuals with IBD remain poorly elucidated, particularly due to a limited number of studies conducted at single-nuclei level. We investigated the dynamics and interactions of cell subtypes during the progression of IBD-associated cancers through comprehensive analysis including single-nuclei transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, ecological dynamic modelling, multiplex immunohistochemistry, in vitro co-culture and in vivo animal studies. The results revealed that CXCL14+ fibroblasts, the primary source of collagen in the microenvironment, play a pivotal role in the inflammation-cancer transition. These fibroblasts progressively increase in abundance during this transition and secreted elevated levels of collagen IV. The increased presence of collagen IV promotes the recruitment and differentiation of SPP1+ macrophages. This interaction ultimately contributes to the development and progression of IBD-associated fibrosis and cancer transformation. Collagen IV, secreted by CXCL14+ fibroblasts, plays a pivotal role in promoting the transition from IBD to cancer. Inhibition of collagen IV secretion not only prevents fibrosis but also hinders the development of inflammation-cancer transition. Our findings are crucial for understanding the mechanisms underlying IBD-associated cancer and developing innovative therapeutic strategies. During the inflammation-cancer transition, activation of the SOX4 leads to increased COL4A1/A2 secretion by CXCL14+ fibroblasts, resulting in enhanced collagen IV synthesis. Collagen IV binds to ITGB1/CD44 receptors on SPP1+ macrophages and activates EGR1/2 to promote SPP1+ macrophage differentiation, while upregulating S100A10 and ANXA2. Activation of S100A10 and ANXA2 promotes recruitment of SPP1+ macrophages, which contributes to immune escape and secretion of oncogenes, thus further promoting fibrosis and tumorigenesis. In addition, SPP1+ macrophages further stimulate CXCL14+ fibroblasts to secrete COL4A1/A2 via TGF-β1, forming a feedback loop that amplifies interactions in the tumour microenvironment.

papers.abstract: Synchronous bilateral primary breast cancer (sBPBC) accounts for 2.9%-3.9% of newly diagnosed breast cancers, while cases with discordant histologic subtypes are exceptionally rare. We report on a 59-year-old woman with synchronous left-sided invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) and right-sided invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC). The patient underwent bilateral breast-conserving surgery with sentinel lymph node biopsy, followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and endocrine therapy. No recurrence or metastasis was observed during the 12-month follow-up. To place the present case in the context of the existing literature, we comparatively reviewed seven previously reported cases of synchronous bilateral IDC and ILC. The comparison illustrated considerable heterogeneity in the clinicopathological characteristics, molecular profiles, nodal involvement, treatment strategies, and clinical outcomes. These findings support independent characterization of each breast lesion and individualized treatment planning based on the features of both tumors.

papers.abstract: Carotid body tumors (CBTs) are rare and highly vascular paragangliomas arising at the carotid bifurcation. Surgical resection remains the standard treatment for CBTs. However, the conventional transcervical approach inevitably leaves a visible cervical scar, which may negatively affect quality of life in patients with cosmetic concerns. A 27-year-old woman presented with a progressively enlarging right neck mass over a 6-month period. Ultrasonography demonstrated a hypervascular lesion surrounding the carotid arteries, and fine-needle aspiration was avoided because of the vascular nature of the tumor. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 4-cm enhancing mass at the carotid bifurcation, highly suggestive of a CBT. Because the patient expressed concern regarding a visible cervical scar, a retroauricular approach was selected after thorough discussion of its potential risks and benefits. The operation was performed by a head and neck surgeon with intraoperative assistance from a vascular surgeon. Complete tumor resection was successfully achieved despite the need for repair of two small arterial defects encountered during tumor mobilization. The operative time was 300 minutes, and the estimated blood loss was 900 mL. The postoperative course was uneventful, and no major complications or tumor recurrence were observed during 12 months of follow-up. The patient reported satisfaction with the cosmetic outcome, although no objective cosmetic assessment was performed. In carefully selected patients with Shamblin type I or II CBT, the retroauricular approach may represent a feasible hidden-scar alternative to the conventional transcervical approach.

papers.abstract: Recurrence remains common after initial transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). This study aimed to identify routinely available clinicopathological, treatment-related, and inflammatory factors associated with recurrence and to characterize recurrence-free survival (RFS). This retrospective cohort included patients with pathologically confirmed Ta, T1, or primary carcinoma in situ (CIS) who underwent initial TURBT between January 2017 and December 2023. Multivariable logistic regression was used as the primary analysis to evaluate factors associated with documented recurrence during follow-up. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed as a complementary analysis incorporating recurrence timing and censoring. Kaplan-Meier analysis, sensitivity analyses, restricted cubic spline analysis, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, and bootstrap-corrected model evaluation were also performed. Among 605 patients, 237 (39.2%) experienced recurrence during a median follow-up of 34.0 months. Multiple tumors were associated with higher recurrence odds and hazard (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.27-2.78; adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.62; 95% CI, 1.25-2.10). Higher recurrence odds and hazards were also associated with increasing tumor diameter, T1 or primary CIS, high-grade pathology, concomitant CIS, and higher baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Maintenance intravesical therapy was inversely associated with recurrence (adjusted OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.34-0.72; adjusted HR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.47-0.81). Estimated RFS rates were 81.5%, 63.8%, and 54.1% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. The bootstrap-corrected area under the curve was 0.769 for the logistic model, and the bootstrap-corrected Harrell's C-index was 0.739 for the Cox model. Recurrence after initial TURBT was associated with greater tumor burden, adverse pathological characteristics, concomitant CIS, and higher baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Maintenance intravesical therapy showed an inverse observational association with recurrence. These routinely available factors may support postoperative risk stratification and risk-adapted surveillance.

papers.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) has become an increasingly popular tool in cancer care over the years. It shows promise in areas like pain management, psychological support, surgical training, and rehabilitation. Even though more studies are being done, there has not been a thorough analysis of the research trends in this field. This study looks at how VR interventions in cancer research have evolved over the past two decades, identifies research hotspots, and explores future directions. We collected publications related to VR in cancer research from the Web of Science Core Collection and Pubmed, covering the period from 2005 to 2025. Using VOSviewer and CiteSpace software, we performed bibliometric and visual analyses. These included examining publication trends, contributions by countries and institutions, author collaboration networks, journal impact, keyword co-occurrence, and citation bursts. A total of 1,259 publications from 110 countries were included. The number of publications fluctuated over time but generally increased, reaching its highest point in 2024 with 184 articles. The United States and China were the most active countries. Jordan had the highest average number of citations per paper. Among institutions, McGill University published the most papers, followed by the University of Toronto. The most productive journal was Surgical Endoscopy and Other Interventional Techniques, whilst Cancers and Supportive Care in Cancer showed the fastest growth. Main research themes included pain management, anxiety reduction, breast cancer, and surgical training. Emerging trends involve the combination of augmented reality (AR), digital health, and artificial intelligence (AI) with VR. This study shows that VR research in cancer care is expanding worldwide, with most contributions coming from North America and Europe. Pain management remains the most common application. New technologies such as AR, AI, and telemedicine are becoming more integrated into VR interventions.

papers.abstract: To investigate the clinical efficacy, safety and prognostic influencing factors of carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) in patients with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC). The clinical data of 39 patients with LS-SCLC who received CIRT from June 2020 to August 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Survival outcomes and adverse reactions were evaluated, and Cox regression was used to analyze prognostic factors. All patients completed the treatment. The 3-month objective response rate (ORR) was 64.10%. The 1- and 2-year local control rates were both 91.2%. The 1- and 2-year overall survival (OS) rates were 91.65% and 62.45%, with a median OS of 44 months. The 1- and 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 72.00% and 47.77%, with a median PFS of 24 months. Serum levels of NSE, CYFRA21-1, SCC and CEA decreased significantly after treatment. Acute treatment-related adverse reactions were mainly grade I-II and could be relieved after symptomatic treatment. Stratified Cox regression indicated that KPS score was an independent protective factor for OS. Univariate analysis suggested that the magnitude of post-treatment reduction in SCC and CYFRA21-1 was potentially associated with survival outcomes. CIRT achieves favorable local tumor control with low acute radiotherapy-related toxicity, and can serve as an alternative therapeutic option for LS-SCLC. This is a single-center, small-sample retrospective study, and the conclusions regarding efficacy and prognosis need to be further verified in larger-sample cohorts.

papers.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) outcomes have improved with proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs, anti-CD38 antibodies, and transplantation, yet a subset of patients with high-risk MM (HRMM) continues to relapse early and die prematurely. Immune effector therapies (IET)-B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)- and G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member D (GPRC5D)-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cells (CAR-T) and bispecific antibodies-have transformed the treatment of relapsed/refractory MM. However, their benefit in HRMM remains incompletely defined. This review describes how HRMM is defined in the IET-era distinguishing baseline biological/genomic risk, clinical high-risk phenotypes, and IET-specific adverse predictors. The International Myeloma Society/International Myeloma Working Group consensus integrates adverse cytogenetics and beta-2 microglobulin, whereas functional high-risk disease, extramedullary disease (EMD), plasma cell leukemia (PCL), high tumor burden, inflammation, and prior BCMA exposure identify aggressive disease in relapsed patients. Across pivotal trials, CAR-T therapy, particularly ciltacabtagene autoleucel, and selected bispecific antibodies retain activity in high-risk cytogenetic subgroups, whereas EMD and PCL remain associated with inferior responses and short progression-free survival. Emerging dual-antigen and trispecific engagers, along with novel targets such as FcRH5 and CD70, aim to overcome antigen escape. Prospective, biology-informed studies are needed to achieve durable disease control in HRMM.

papers.abstract: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumor of the kidney (MEST) is a rare renal neoplasm with biphasic differentiation comprising epithelial and stromal components. It typically appears as a mixed cystic-solid mass on imaging, and the prognosis is favorable in the vast majority of cases. We report a case of MEST with a prominent fat component on imaging: a 54-year-old woman was admitted with a 1-month history of left flank distension and pain. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed a mixed cystic-solid mass at the lower pole of the left kidney, with a prominent low-attenuation fat-density area surrounding the mass. Preoperatively, the lesion was considered an unusual angiomyolipoma with epithelial cysts (AMLEC). Because the lesion was small, located at the lower pole, and relatively well circumscribed, the patient underwent laparoscopic left partial nephrectomy. Postoperative histopathologic examination confirmed that the left renal mass was benign; however, immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrated positivity for EMA and PCK in the epithelial component and for PR and ER in the stromal component, supporting a diagnosis of MEST. The adipose tissue submitted separately with the tumor was located around the tumor and could not be definitively confirmed as an intratumoral component. This case demonstrates that MEST may also exhibit prominent adipose tissue on imaging and illustrates the diagnostic pitfall in which fat-related imaging findings cause MEST to mimic AMLEC, making the early distinction between MEST and cystic change in fat-containing renal tumors challenging.

papers.abstract: age and ovarian reserve markers are commonly used in clinical practice to predict ovarian response to controlled stimulation for assisted reproductive techniques in infertile patients. In oncofertility, some reports suggest the predictive performance of these markers may be lower in specific subgroups. We evaluated the performance of a prespecified age + log(AMH) model for predicting metaphase-II (MII) oocyte yield in women undergoing oocyte cryopreservation before gonadotoxic treatment. This retrospective single-center cohort study included consecutive oocyte cryopreservation cycles performed before gonadotoxic treatment between January 2015 and January 2025. MII yield was modelled using negative-binomial regression with age and log-transformed AMH as predictors. Regression coefficients were estimated in the current cohort. Model performance was assessed using calibration measures and patient-level bootstrap internal validation, with all cycles from the same woman kept together during resampling. Analyses were performed overall and by cancer type. Threshold-based underestimation analyses and the incremental value of antral follicle count (AFC) were also explored. A total of 179 oocyte cryopreservation cycles performed in 167 women were included. The model showed good overall calibration using aggregated out-of-bootstrap predictions, with calibration-in-the-large of 0.00 (95% CI -0.08 to 0.09) and calibration slope of 0.98 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.15). Mean prediction error was -0.10 MII (95% CI -0.97 to 0.80), indicating minimal average directional bias. Mean absolute error was 4.12 MII (95% CI 3.53 to 4.76), and root mean squared error was 5.94 MII (95% CI 4.92 to 7.00). Substantial underestimation, defined as observed MII yield exceeding predicted yield by more than 4 MII, was more frequent in hematologic malignancies than in solid tumors (31.8% [14/44] vs 12.6% [17/135]; risk difference +19.2 percentage points, 95% CI + 4.4 to +34.1; Fisher's exact p=0.006). This finding remained consistent in the one-cycle-per-woman sensitivity analysis. Adding AFC did not improve predictive performance in the complete-case analysis. age and AMH are useful tools for counseling regarding the expected mature oocyte yield, including in our subset of oncofertility patients. As we found substantial underestimation of mature oocyte yield to be more frequent in hematologic malignancies, the results should be interpreted cautiously in this subgroup.

papers.abstract: Inflammatory markers have been reported to be associated with outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, whether early treatment-related changes in these markers provide additional prognostic information remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between dynamic changes in peripheral blood inflammatory markers during chemotherapy and survival outcomes in patients with NSCLC. We retrospectively analyzed 479 patients with NSCLC who received chemotherapy. Changes in lymphocyte, platelet, and neutrophil counts, as well as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), were calculated as absolute differences (D-values) between baseline measurements obtained before the first chemotherapy session and post-chemotherapy measurements obtained within 7 days after the first session. Overall survival (OS) was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Additional Cox models were used to examine the association of PLR D-value with OS after accounting for baseline PLR and clinical covariates. A prognostic nomogram was constructed as an exploratory risk-estimation model. Greater changes in the evaluated hematological markers were associated with shorter OS in Kaplan-Meier analysis. In the primary multivariable Cox regression, high PLR D-value was associated with shorter OS (hazard ratio, 1.422; 95% confidence interval, 1.001-2.020; P = 0.049), together with sex, anemia status, and tumor extent. After adjustment for baseline PLR and clinical covariates, however, PLR D-value was no longer significantly associated with OS when analyzed either as a continuous variable (HR per 50-unit increase, 1.010; 95% CI, 0.947-1.078; P = 0.762) or using the original high/low classification (HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.91-1.89; P = 0.145). The nomogram had an apparent C-index of 0.630 and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.618 after 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Greater changes in PLR during chemotherapy were associated with shorter OS in the primary categorical analysis. However, this association was attenuated after baseline PLR and clinical factors were taken into account, indicating that the additional prognostic contribution of PLR D-value may be limited. The nomogram should be considered exploratory and requires external validation before clinical application.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic hamartoma (PH) is an exceedingly rare benign non-neoplastic lesion of the pancreas. Owing to its nonspecific clinical and radiological features, it is prone to misdiagnosis. Among its various subtypes, functionally active pancreatic hamartomas with distinct endocrine activity have only been sporadically reported in the literature as individual cases. We report the case of a 58-year-old female patient whose initial presentation was characterized by paroxysmal behavioral abnormalities during nocturnal sleep, manifesting as sudden agitation, arm-flinging, and purposeless stereotyped movements after sleep onset. During these episodes, the patient exhibited a confusional state with subsequent complete amnesia for the events, a clinical phenotype highly suggestive of REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) or frontal lobe epilepsy. In-hospital monitoring revealed refractory nocturnal hypoglycemia. Imaging studies identified a mass in the pancreatic tail, and the patient underwent laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy. Postoperative histopathological and immunohistochemical examination confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic hamartoma, composed predominantly of islet cells (approximately 90%) with associated islet cell tumor-like hyperplasia. Following surgery, the patient's nocturnal hypoglycemia and sleep-related behavioral abnormalities resolved completely.

papers.abstract: Abscess-like presentations are common in surgical practice, but malignant soft-tissue and lymphoid disorders can occasionally imitate infection and delay definitive treatment. Anaplastic large-cell lymphoma (ALCL) is a CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma that may involve skin, lymph nodes, or soft tissue and can show extensive necrosis, inflammatory change, and systemic symptoms. A 17-year-old female student presented with a 3-week history of progressive painful erythema and swelling of the left axilla after ineffective intravenous antibiotic treatment elsewhere. On admission, the lesion was large, indurated, tender, and clinically suspicious for a soft-tissue infection with possible abscess formation. Incision and drainage yielded only scant purulent fluid but abundant friable nodular tissue, and cultures were negative. Persistent fever, local progression, lymphadenopathy, and poor response to antimicrobial therapy prompted multidisciplinary reassessment. Histopathology of the solid tissue demonstrated large pleomorphic lymphoid cells, and immunohistochemistry showed strong CD30 and ALK expression, establishing ALK-positive ALCL. The patient was transferred to hematology and received initial cytoreductive therapy with brentuximab vedotin and short-course zeprumetostat, after which the local tumor burden decreased and delayed wound closure was performed. She subsequently received five cycles of brentuximab vedotin plus CHP and chidamide maintenance after complete remission. A presumed abscess that yields little pus but contains solid friable tissue should not be managed as infection alone. In refractory, culture-negative, or biologically discordant soft-tissue lesions, early biopsy of the cavity wall and solid components may help reduce diagnostic delay and redirect care toward malignancy-specific treatment.

papers.abstract: Mismatch repair deficiency defines an immunologically distinct subgroup of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, but its relationship with CD163-positive macrophage infiltration in early-stage disease remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between MMR status and quantitative CD163-positive TAM infiltration, together with secondary clinicopathologic and exploratory DFS analyses. This single-center retrospective cohort included patients with surgically treated FIGO 2009 stage I-II endometrioid endometrial carcinoma and available formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumor tissue. Immunohistochemistry for MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6, and CD163 defined MMR status and quantified macrophage density. CD163-positive TAM density was analyzed quantitatively as the principal measure, with a cohort-median low/high categorization retained for secondary phenotypic analyses. Median regression evaluated the association between MMR status and continuous CD163-positive TAM density, whereas logistic regression was used for the secondary binary TAM analysis and the composite adverse pathologic endpoint. Exploratory DFS analyses included single-marker and combined Cox models, formal MMR-by-TAM interaction testing, and comparison of models with and without continuous CD163-positive TAM density. Among 254 patients assessed, 236 were included. MMR protein expression was retained in 172 tumors (72.9%), whereas 64 (27.1%) were classified as dMMR. CD163-positive TAM density was higher in dMMR than pMMR tumors (median, 76 vs 47 cells/HPF; P<0.001), and high TAM infiltration was more frequent in dMMR tumors (44/64, 68.8% vs 71/172, 41.3%; P<0.001). After adjustment for age, FIGO stage, tumor grade, tumor size, and deep myometrial invasion, dMMR remained associated with high macrophage infiltration (adjusted OR, 2.27; 95% CI, 1.19-4.18; P = 0.008). High macrophage infiltration was associated with grade 3 histology, deep myometrial invasion, LVSI, and the composite adverse pathologic feature; the association with the composite endpoint persisted after adjustment (adjusted OR, 1.78; 95% CI, 1.01-3.14; P = 0.047). During follow-up, 26 DFS events occurred. In exploratory Cox analyses, dMMR was associated with DFS (adjusted HR, 2.76; 95% CI, 1.25-6.10; P = 0.012), whereas continuous CD163-positive TAM density was not (adjusted HR per 10 cells/HPF, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.97-1.12; P = 0.281), and addition of CD163-positive TAM density did not significantly improve model fit beyond MMR status (likelihood-ratio P = 0.279). The dMMR/high-TAM phenotype retained an exploratory association with DFS in the conventional model (adjusted HR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.02-4.81; P = 0.044), but the association was attenuated after additional adjustment for adjuvant therapy (HR, 2.04; 95% CI, 0.93-4.52; P = 0.075). IHC-defined dMMR was associated with increased CD163-positive macrophage infiltration, and higher TAM infiltration was associated with adverse pathologic features. DFS findings were exploratory and did not establish incremental prognostic value of CD163-positive TAM infiltration beyond MMR status; larger externally validated cohorts are required to assess prognostic relevance.

papers.abstract: In colorectal cancer, the AJCC T category is defined by the depth of bowel wall invasion rather than by the absolute size of the primary tumor. The clinical value of tumor size in assessing tumor aggressiveness, metastatic risk, and prognosis remains insufficiently investigated. To evaluate the clinical value of tumor size in assessing potential metastatic risk and prognostic stratification in colorectal cancer. We retrospectively included 10,513 patients with colorectal cancer who underwent surgical treatment at FUSCC between 2008 and 2020. We integrated tumor size with clinicopathological characteristics to assess metastatic risk using machine-learning models and SHAP-based interpretation. By modeling tumor size as both a categorical and continuous variable, we further investigated its prognostic relevance using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression incorporating restricted cubic splines. Additionally, an independent cohort of 6,739 patients from Changhai Hospital was used for external validation. Machine-learning identified lymph node metastasis as the primary predictive endpoint, with the CatBoost model achieving the highest AUROC of 0.800. SHAP analysis showed that smaller tumor diameter contributed positively to predicted metastatic risk. Multivariable restricted cubic spline analysis further demonstrated a significant nonlinear association between tumor diameter and OS, with mortality risk increasing as tumor diameter decreased within the approximately 0-3 cm range. Among younger male patients with locally advanced disease, tumors ≤3 cm were associated with significantly worse OS and DFS than tumors >5 cm (both P < 0.001). External validation yielded similar findings. Smaller tumor size may paradoxically indicate higher lymph node metastatic risk and poorer prognosis in a subset of patients with colorectal cancer, particularly younger male patients with locally advanced disease. Tumor size may therefore serve as a complementary factor for postoperative risk stratification beyond conventional TNM staging.

papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains a major clinical challenge because of delayed diagnosis and the lack of validated non-invasive biomarkers for OSCC detection. Epigenetic alterations during oral carcinogenesis represent promising biomarker candidates. This study aimed to prioritize clinically relevant epigenetic biomarkers and validate EPHA5 using an integrated genome-wide DNA methylation and transcriptomic approach. Genome-wide DNA methylation and transcriptomic profiling were performed to identify epigenetically deregulated genes in OSCC. Candidate genes were prioritized by integrating DNA methylation, transcriptomic data and biological relevance. EPHA5 was subsequently selected for validation and evaluated by quantitative methylation-specific PCR (QMSP) and quantitative real-time PCR (QRT-PCR) in tissue, saliva and serum samples from independent cohorts comprising patients with OSCC, oral premalignant lesions (OPML) and healthy controls. Genome-wide analysis identified 661 upregulated and 577 downregulated genes together with 2,431 differentially methylated regions corresponding to 1,776 genes. Integrated analysis generated a panel of 51 candidate genes, from which EPHA5 was prioritized using integrated DNA methylation, gene expression, pathway enrichment and biological relevance. EPHA5 promoter hypermethylation was detected in 66.7% of OSCC tumors, whereas concurrent promoter hypermethylation and reduced expression were observed in 28.6% of tumors. Methylation was also detected in 54.5% of OPML lesions and in the saliva of 47.6% of OSCC patients but was rarely detected in healthy controls. Tumor EPHA5 methylation significantly discriminated OSCC from healthy controls (AUC = 0.780, p = 0.004; sensitivity, 71.4%; specificity, 75%). Salivary EPHA5 methylation also significantly discriminated OSCC from healthy controls (AUC = 0.717, p = 0.025; sensitivity, 52.4%; specificity, 87.5%), whereas serum methylation showed no significant diagnostic utility (AUC = 0.571, p = 0.462). Discrimination between OSCC and OPML was limited and did not reach statistical significance (tumor AUC = 0.662, p = 0.068; salivary AUC = 0.600, p = 0.264). Frequent tumor hypermethylation together with detectable salivary methylation supports further evaluation of EPHA5 as a candidate non-invasive epigenetic biomarker for OSCC. However, its moderate diagnostic performance, limited discrimination between OSCC and OPML, and lack of external validation indicate that larger prospective studies and evaluation within multimarker methylation panels are required before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: In oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), body mass index (BMI) is an available but imperfect marker of nutritional reserve. Evidence on pretreatment BMI in surgery-based European OSCC cohorts remains limited, especially regarding perioperative outcomes. This study evaluated associations of pretreatment BMI with overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and perioperative outcomes after curative-intent R0 resection. This retrospective single-center cohort included adult patients with previously untreated primary OSCC, available pretreatment BMI, and curative-intent R0 surgery between 2014 and 2023. BMI was assessed continuously and by World Health Organization (WHO) categories. OS and RFS were analyzed using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, pathological T category, nodal status, microvascular free-flap reconstruction, and diabetes mellitus. Perioperative outcomes included red blood cell (RBC) transfusion, RBC units transfused, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) placement, and intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay. A total of 274 patients with available pretreatment BMI were included; 116 deaths occurred. Five-year OS ranged from 31.4% in patients classified as underweight to 82.0% in patients with obesity. Higher BMI was associated with lower mortality (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99; p = 0.013), and obesity was associated with improved OS compared with normal weight (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.26-0.96; p = 0.037). BMI was not significantly associated with RFS after adjustment (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.97, 95% CI 0.93-1.00; p = 0.080). Higher BMI was associated with fewer perioperative RBC transfusions (any transfusion: OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.98; p = 0.012; number of units: OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.95; p = 0.001). BMI was not independently associated with PEG placement or hospital length of stay; ICU findings depended on BMI modeling. Higher pretreatment BMI was associated with better OS and lower perioperative RBC transfusion requirements, whereas associations with RFS and most other perioperative outcomes were not significant after adjustment. Given the retrospective design and limitations of BMI as a body-composition marker, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Pretreatment BMI may help identify low-BMI patients warranting early supportive-care assessment.

papers.abstract: Multiple prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET tracers are used for patient selection in radioligand therapy (RLT). This study compared treatment response to RLT across different PSMA tracers. We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent Lu-177 PSMA-617 RLT with baseline imaging using either Ga-68 PSMA-11 or F-18 DCFPyL PET. PET parameters were measured, including SUVmean, SUVmax, and total tumor volume (TTV). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with PSA50 response, and Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with overall survival. Of 140 patients analyzed (Ga-68 PSMA-11: n=51; F-18 DCFPyL: n=89), SUVmax and SUVmean did not differ significantly between groups; however, TTV was significantly higher in the Ga-68 PSMA-11 group (p=0.038). In multivariable analysis adjusted for age, baseline PSA, PET tracer type, SUVmean, and log-transformed TTV, PET tracer type was not significantly associated with PSA50 response (OR, 1.318; 95% CI, 0.585-2.970; p=0.505), whereas higher SUVmean was associated with greater odds of PSA50 response (OR, 1.285; 95% CI, 1.126-1.466; p<0.001). Overall survival did not differ significantly between tracer groups (HR, 0.760; 95% CI, 0.507-1.138; p=0.183), with median overall survival of 8.4 and 12.6 months. In multivariable analysis, PET tracer type was not significantly associated with overall survival (HR, 0.736; 95% CI, 0.475-1.139; p=0.168), whereas higher SUVmean was associated with a lower risk of death (HR, 0.886; 95% CI, 0.825-0.950; p<0.001) and higher log-transformed TTV was associated with a higher risk of death (HR, 1.415; 95% CI, 1.194-1.678; p<0.001). PET tracer type was not significantly associated with PSA50 response or overall survival following RLT. Higher SUVmean was associated with greater odds of PSA50 response and a lower risk of death, whereas higher TTV was associated with overall survival.

papers.abstract: We report the management of a 36-year-old man presenting with rapidly progressive and highly symptomatic cutaneous metastases (CMs) from metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). He was referred to palliative radiotherapy because of painful and pruritic skin lesions. His history included two synchronous colorectal adenocarcinomas. Comprehensive next-generation sequencing identified the rectosigmoid tumor as the metastatic source and revealed a pathogenic germline BRCA1 mutation, supporting a precision systemic strategy (olaparib plus pembrolizumab). CMs were the patient's dominant source of morbidity and progressively involved new skin sites; the patient therefore, received three sequential courses of helical tomotherapy (Radixact®), each delivering 30 Gy in 10 fractions to extended superficial volumes exceeding 50 cm. Each course treated adjacent fields with limited high-dose overlap. Deformable co-registration with the prior plans and cumulative-dose review confirmed that the high-dose overlap was limited, distinguishing this approach from re-irradiation. A posterior skin strip was consistently spared to preserve lymphatic drainage and reduce the risk of compartment toxicity. All three courses produced a very good partial response (VGPR) at six weeks, with toxicity limited to grade 1 dermatitis (no grade ≥2). Crucially, repeated irradiation maintained durable symptom control, avoided escalation of opioid analgesia for approximately six months, and allowed continuation of the same systemic regimen for nine months until lung progression. This case illustrates that iterative skin-directed radiotherapy can deliver safe, repeatable, high-quality palliation in extensive CMs.

papers.abstract: MYH9 is upregulated in various malignancies, but its role in breast cancer chemoresistance remains unclear. We investigated whether MYH9 regulates doxorubicin (ADR) resistance via GRP78 stabilization and PERK pathway modulation. MYH9 expression was analyzed in breast cancer tissues and cell lines by immunohistochemistry and western blot. ADR-resistant MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 cell lines were established. MYH9 knockdown/overexpression and GRP78 overexpression were achieved by lentiviral transduction. Protein interactions, degradation assays, PERK signaling, apoptosis, and in vivo drug responses were evaluated. MYH9 was significantly upregulated in breast cancer tissues, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (95.2%), and further elevated in ADR-resistant cells. MYH9 overexpression enhanced ADR tolerance, while knockdown sensitized resistant cells in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, MYH9 directly bound GRP78 (but not CALR or GRP94), inhibiting ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation. MYH9 depletion reduced GRP78 levels and activated the PERK pathway (p-eIF2α, ATF4, CHOP), promoting apoptosis via Bax/Bad upregulation and Bcl-2 downregulation. ERS induction with thapsigargin enhanced ADR sensitivity, whereas 4-PBA attenuated it. GRP78 overexpression rescued ADR resistance, confirming GRP78 dependency. MYH9 confers ADR resistance in breast cancer by stabilizing GRP78 and suppressing PERK-driven apoptosis, identifying the MYH9/GRP78 axis as a potential therapeutic target for overcoming chemoresistance.

papers.abstract: To characterise age-related gradients in colorectal lesion severity and prespecified high-risk endoscopic features in a lesion-confirmed screening colonoscopy cohort and to evaluate an investigator-defined red-flag composite as an exploratory marker of advanced pathology. Helicobacter pylori was assessed as a secondary exposure. This retrospective cohort included 291 participants with histologically confirmed lesions in four age groups (36-45, 46-55, 56-65 and 66-72 years). Logistic regression evaluated predictors of advanced neoplasia (high-grade dysplasia [HGD] or adenocarcinoma); adenocarcinoma-only and age × H. pylori interaction analyses were exploratory because events were sparse. With advancing age, body mass index, H. pylori positivity, adenoma, sessile serrated lesions, HGD, adenocarcinoma and high-risk endoscopic features increased, whereas hyperplastic polyps decreased (all P < 0.05). Age (per 10 years), male sex, H. pylori positivity, lesion size ≥10 mm, proximal location and JNET 2B/3 pattern were independently associated with advanced neoplasia. Red-flag positivity (≥2 of four features) increased from 5.2% to 32.7% and enriched for adenocarcinoma, although positive predictive values were imprecise and non-monotonic. Colorectal lesion severity and high-risk endoscopic features showed an age-related gradient. The red-flag composite is an exploratory descriptive construct, not a validated predictive score. H. pylori findings, especially interaction analyses, are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma CNS WHO Grade 4 (GBM) is associated with poor prognosis and high recurrence rates despite the current therapeutic approaches. Conventional imaging, in particular Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), is primarily used during follow-up to detect tumor recurrence but has limited ability to distinguish recurrence from therapy-related changes, such as tissue necrosis and postoperative scar tissue. Liquid biopsy using circulating tumor-specific serological biomarkers, such as miRNAs, provides a gene expression signature for early identification of GBM recurrence. This pilot "proof-of-concept" study investigated the potential of circulating tumor-derived miRNA in whole blood samples for early detection of tumor recurrence. In a previous whole-transcriptome screening (NGS) study, whole-blood samples (n = 33) from seven patients and tumor biopsies (n = 4) were used to identify biomarkers. Corresponding to tumor surgery and recurrence, miRNA expression was examined in pre-surgical blood samples and tumor tissues. In whole blood, we investigated whether a pattern could be identified indicating post-surgery downregulation, consistent with reduced tumor burden, followed by a return to pre-surgery levels at recurrence. We identified 1-19 miRNA species per patient (a total of 72 miRNAs) showing this pattern. In this manuscript, we present the qRT-PCR validation results. The 45 most promising miRNAs identified by NGS study were selected and quantified using qRT-PCR. In addition, miR-21 was included as a promising candidate reported in the literature. To address challenges in miRNA normalization, five normalization strategies and unnormalized raw Ct values were compared. Two normalization approaches (median DCt normalization and unnormalized raw Ct values) showed no systematic bias. Depending on the normalization method, the agreement between NGS and qRT-PCR ranged from 23.6 to 27.9%. Although the concordance between NGS and qRT-PCR was low at the individual-patient level, qRT-PCR identified a common set of 24 miRNAs differentially regulated across patients. Notably, miR-424-3p and miR-362-5p were shared by five of seven patients, followed by miR-1307-3p and miR-22-5p, each shared by four patients. Interestingly, miR-21 did not show the predefined recurrence-associated pattern in any patient. Blood-based miRNA profiling may complement imaging in longitudinal monitoring of GBM patients, although clinical benefits have not been confirmed, and validation in a larger independent cohort is required.

papers.abstract: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-based adaptive radiotherapy (ART) has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing inter-fractional anatomical and physiological changes during treatment. By incorporating on-treatment imaging, ART enables treatment plans to be adapted to the anatomy of the day, with the potential to improve target coverage and reduce dose exposure to organs at risk (OARs). However, routine implementation remains constrained by the limited image quality of CBCT, uncertainties in dose calculation, labour-intensive workflows and the lack of reliable criteria for determining when adaptation is clinically necessary. This review summarises the development, current status and future prospects of CBCT-based ART, with particular emphasis on artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted automated delineation and automated radiotherapy decision-making systems. CBCT is widely available on modern linear accelerators and remains the most practical imaging basis for ART in many centres. Nevertheless, poor soft-tissue contrast, noise, artefacts, field-of-view truncation and unstable Hounsfield unit values limit its performance in target delineation and dose reconstruction. Recent advances in image-quality enhancement, deformable image registration and synthetic CT generation have partially addressed these limitations. AI-based auto-segmentation models, including convolutional neural networks, Transformers, generative adversarial networks and diffusion models, have demonstrated increasingly favourable geometric accuracy and workflow efficiency. Automated decision-making systems can advise clinicians whether treatment-plan adaptation is required and how it should be implemented according to each patient's circumstances, representing a prerequisite for more efficient ART. Current research has mainly focused on two approaches: adaptation triggered by predefined dosimetric thresholds, and artificial-intelligence-based models that learn from prior knowledge and predict potential dosimetric changes for the current patient based on previous experience. Both approaches have their respective strengths and limitations, but require further refinement, including the systematic exploration of decision thresholds. Moreover, the realisation of fully automated adaptive radiotherapy will require the integration of additional systems, including automated treatment planning and automated QA. Overall, CBCT-based ART assisted by AI is technically feasible and may improve dosimetric quality and treatment efficiency. Future progress requires improved CBCT-specific algorithms, integrated automated planning and QA, multicentre validation, standardised safety frameworks and stronger evidence of clinical benefit.

papers.abstract: Aberrant promoter DNA methylation represents an early molecular alteration in oral carcinogenesis and has emerged as a potential source of molecular biomarkers for oral cancer. Although RNF152 has been implicated in cancer-related molecular dysregulation, its promoter methylation and expression status have not previously been specifically investigated in oral premalignant lesions (OPML) or oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). RNF152 promoter methylation and gene expression were evaluated in paired tumor/lesion and matched adjacent normal tissues from 30 patients with OSCC and 30 patients with OPML, together with oral mucosal tissues from 15 healthy controls. Matched saliva and serum samples from the patient cohorts were also analyzed to evaluate RNF152 methylation as a potential liquid biopsy marker. Quantitative methylation-specific PCR (QMSP) and quantitative real-time PCR (QRT-PCR) were performed, and associations with clinicopathological characteristics, diagnostic performance, and the relationship between promoter methylation and gene expression were investigated. RNF152 promoter methylation was detected in 36.7% of OSCC tumors and 70.0% of OPML lesions, whereas no promoter methylation was identified in oral mucosal tissues from healthy controls. Promoter methylation was also detected in matched saliva and serum samples from both patient groups. Reduced RNF152 expression was observed in 33.3% of OSCC and 30.0% of OPML tissues. Methylation-associated RNF152 expression loss was identified in 13.3% of OSCC and 30.0% of OPML patients. Among methylation-positive cases, concomitant RNF152 expression loss was observed in 36.4% of patients with OSCC and 42.9% of patients with OPML. Continuous promoter methylation levels were not significantly correlated with tissue gene expression in either cohort. RNF152 promoter methylation demonstrated good discriminatory performance for distinguishing OPML from healthy controls (AUC = 0.867, p < 0.001), whereas its discriminatory performance for OSCC was statistically significant but more modest (AUC = 0.683, p = 0.047). This study provides the first comprehensive evaluation of RNF152 promoter methylation and gene expression in oral premalignant lesions and oral squamous cell carcinoma. RNF152 promoter methylation showed greater diagnostic potential for OPML than for OSCC, whereas its performance in liquid biopsy specimens was limited. The incomplete concordance between promoter methylation and gene expression suggests that promoter methylation may contribute to RNF152 downregulation in a subset of cases but is not the sole determinant of its expression. These findings support further evaluation of RNF152 as a candidate component of multimarker epigenetic panels rather than as a standalone diagnostic biomarker. Validation in larger, independent cohorts is required to determine its clinical utility.

papers.abstract: Innate immune signaling through inflammasome activation has been implicated in the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis (MS). We previously demonstrated that nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs), drugs approved to treat HIV and hepatitis B virus infections, and kamuvudines, safer NRTI derivatives, both inhibit inflammasome activation. Here, we report that in the experimental autoimmune encephalitis mouse model of MS, treatment with kamuvudine-9 (K-9), an NRTI derivative with an enhanced safety profile, prevented further neurological deficits and reversed preexisting paralysis and vision loss. K-9 promoted myelin and axonal preservation in the mouse spinal cord and abolished the increase in serum neurofilament light (NfL) chain. K-9 disrupted interactions between nucleotide-binding domain leucine-rich repeat (NLR) pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) and NIMA-related kinase 7 (NEK7) and between NLRP3 and NLR CARD domain containing 4 (NLRC4), inhibiting dual inflammasome activation. K-9 also exhibited appropriate safety and pharmacokinetic characteristics and biodistribution. In three distinct human cohorts, there was a lower incidence of MS in those individuals receiving NRTIs for HIV infection, preexposure prophylaxis for HIV, or hepatitis B virus infection. NRTI use was also associated with a reduction in relapse rate in individuals with MS. These findings provide a rationale for further investigating K-9 for treating MS.
