papers.abstract: Conversion therapy may create an opportunity for liver resection in selected patients with initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but reported conversion rates use heterogeneous denominators and endpoints. We estimated actual completed hepatectomy using a verified all-treated denominator. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library/CENTRAL, Wanfang Data, and CNKI were searched through April 10, 2026. Eligible cohorts included initially or baseline unresectable HCC, an all-treated denominator, and completed liver resection events. Two authors independently assessed eligibility, extracted data, and evaluated risk of bias. Random-effects logit proportion meta-analysis, Hartung-Knapp sensitivity, prediction intervals, leave-one-out analyses, treatment-strategy subgroups, publication-year meta-regression, and small-study-effect diagnostics were undertaken. PROSPERO: CRD420261360108. Thirty-seven reports represented 36 unique studies; 34 studies involving 5,137 patients and 1,042 completed hepatectomies entered the quantitative synthesis. The crude aggregate resection rate was 20.3% (1,042/5,137), whereas the random-effects modeled pooled rate was 25.40% (95% CI, 20.74%-30.69%; I2=91.5%; tau2=0.5132). The Hartung-Knapp 95% CI was 20.12%-31.51%, and the prediction interval was 7.16%-60.04%. Leave-one-out estimates ranged from 24.52% to 26.64%. Treatment-strategy differences were not statistically significant (Qm=5.17, df=2, P = 0.075). Publication-year meta-regression did not show a clear linear association (OR per decade 1.19, 95% CI 0.77-1.83; P = 0.440), and Egger's test did not indicate significant funnel asymmetry (P = 0.381). Approximately one-quarter of patients initiating conversion therapy underwent actual hepatectomy, but the crude and modeled estimates differ because substantial heterogeneity changes random-effects study weighting. The pooled estimate is a cross-study, cross-era benchmark for multidisciplinary decision-making rather than a universal patient-level probability or a treatment-specific efficacy estimate. www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261360108.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GB) represents one of the most aggressive primary brain tumors characterized by poor prognosis, high relapse and resistance to conventional therapies. Salidroside, a naturally occurring glucoside derived from Rhodiola rosea, has been reported to exhibit pro-apoptotic and anti-proliferative properties across multiple cancer models; however, its mechanistic basis in glioma and its therapeutic potential remain incompletely characterized. Neuroglobin (Ngb) protein expression was analyzed in 101 glioma brain tissue specimens and 5 normal brain tissues by western blot and immunohistochemical staining. In silico analyses of oxidized and reduced state of Ngb with salidroside was performed along with pharmacokinetics and toxicity predictions to computationally evaluate possible binding interactions and drug-like properties. Further, to determine the underlying mechanisms, in vitro assays were performed in U87MG and LN229 human glioblastoma cells treated with salidroside. MTT assay, transwell assay, Annexin V/PI staining, mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), CYP2E1 activity, intracellular NADPH levels, Fe2+/Fe3+ ratio and markers of oxidative stress including ROS assay and lipid peroxidation were also measured. The mechanism of Ngb aided apoptosis was investigated by protein expression of Ngb, caspase 3 and cytosolic cytochrome c in glioma cells. Ngb expression in glioma tissues samples significantly downregulated with increasing tumour grade as determined by immunoreactivity and western blot analysis. In-silico analyses predicted a possible interaction of salidroside with reduced state of Ngb, In vitro studies suggested significant reduction in cell viability, migration and invasion in both U87MG and LN229 cells on supplementation with salidroside. These effects were accompanied by increased CYP2E1 activity, altered intracellular NADPH levels indicating induction of oxidative stress. Mitochondrial dysfunction, manifested as reduced MMP, elevated lipid peroxidation and increased cytosolic cytochrome c release indicated activation of intrinsic apoptotic pathway. Computational analyses additionally predicted a preferential interaction with the reduced form of Ngb, providing a mechanistic hypothesis warranting experimental validation. Salidroside exerts multi-faceted anti-cancer effects in glioblastoma cells, potentially involving upregulation of Ngb levels in glioma cells, modulation of redox homeostasis, mitochondrial integrity and intrinsic apoptotic signaling.

papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics resolves tissue organization in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), whereas most clinically annotated cohorts remain bulk transcriptomic datasets. We evaluated six literature-informed curated composite programs across bulk, single-cell and spatial datasets without assuming a discrete ecosystem taxonomy. The programs comprised Macrophage-rich, T cell-inflamed, Antigen-presentation, Stromal/fibrotic, Immune-cold/exclusion and Proliferative/cycling, with 22 memberships per program (132 memberships, 121 unique genes and 11 shared memberships). In 498 GSE31312 tumors, principal components 1 and 2 (PC1 and PC2) explained 48.6% and 20.8% of score variance. No candidate discrete taxonomy demonstrated sufficient stability for retention; k=2 met silhouette and size criteria but failed both bootstrap-stability thresholds. Historical 15-edge concordance was high for GSE10846 (rho=0.936) and GSE181063 (rho=0.982), whereas the most restrictive GSE10846 edge-exclusion sensitivity, removing both shared-gene and proliferation-associated edges, reduced rho to 0.690. Single-cell analysis of 14,368 DLBCL cells from four patients and eight samples provided descriptive lineage context. In Visium V2 areas, the antigen-presentation series was treated as AP-residual (HLA-unmeasured) because only 13/22 program genes were measurable and all nine HLA genes in the defined program were unavailable. Matched-random-gene-set support was broad but not universal (24/30 DLBCL, 18/24 context/background, 42/54 overall; 25/32 primary-plus-exploratory), whereas both depth-adjusted residual endpoints were supported in 30/30 DLBCL area-program combinations. These findings support continuous program-level interpretation while retaining explicit provenance, stability, assay, method and sampling limitations.

papers.abstract: Small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SI-NETs) are characterized by a low mutational burden and limited recurrent driver mutations, suggesting that other mechanisms contribute to tumor development. One of the most frequent genomic alterations in SI-NETs is loss of heterozygosity on chromosome 18 (chr18del), which defines a major molecular subtype. However, the epigenetic consequences of this event remain poorly understood. In this study, we used long-read whole-genome sequencing to characterize genome-wide DNA methylation patterns in twelve primary tumors. Native methylation detection and copy-number profiling enabled stratification of tumors according to chromosome 18 status and direct comparison of epigenetic states between chr18del and non-chr18del (diploid) tumors. Chr18del tumors displayed widespread hypomethylation relative to diploid tumors, while chromosome 18 showed spatially structured regional methylation differences, including localized regions of increased methylation. Cross-platform validation using an independent Illumina EPIC methylation cohort confirmed the direction and distribution of many methylation events. Integration with the corresponding transcriptomic dataset revealed that a subset of methylation changes was associated with differential gene expression consistent with established promoter- and gene-body methylation models. Functional categorization of these methylation states revealed regulatory patterns linked to neuronal signaling, intracellular signaling cascades, and interactions with the extracellular matrix. Together, these findings support an association between chromosome 18 status and widespread methylation differences that extend beyond the affected chromosome and are linked to transcriptional programs relevant to neuroendocrine tumor biology.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a malignant tumor characterized by high recurrence and metastasis rates, as well as a poor prognosis. Cuproptosis is a form of programmed cell death driven by abnormal copper-ion metabolism. Existing studies have shown that its occurrence is closely regulated and associated with the progression of HCC. However, it is still unclear how long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) control the process in HCC. The purpose of this work is to clarify how the lncRNA AP003469.2 influences cuproptosis and promotes the development of HCC. This study utilized RNA sequencing data from the TCGA-LIHC dataset to screen for cuproptosis-related lncRNAs exhibiting significant expression differences. Following the initial screening, the expression of lncRNA AP003469.2 was validated using qRT-PCR. Subsequent in vitro and in vivo studies confirmed AP003469.2's biological role in HCC. To understand the fundamental mechanisms, we determined the subcellular localization of the proteins using nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). The regulatory relationships between miR-4732-3p and LIPT1 and between AP003469.2 and miR-4732-3p were then verified using dual-luciferase reporter assays. In addition, we utilized Western blotting, copper assays, CCK-8, and immunohistochemistry to evaluate related proteins and markers indicative of cuproptosis. A poor prognosis was observed to be positively correlated with elevated expression of AP003469.2 in HCC. In both in vivo and in vitro experimental methods, AP003469.2 stimulated important malignant characteristics in HCC cells, including invasion, migration, and proliferation. Furthermore, by controlling LIPT1 expression and modulating copper homeostasis and important proteins, including FDX1, SLC31A1, and HSP70, AP003469.2 acts as a molecular sponge for miR-4732-3p, attenuating cuproptosis. Our research demonstrated that the AP003469.2/miR-4732-3p/LIPT1 axis could suppress cuproptosis to promote HCC progression. Therefore, AP003469.2 may serve as a target for HCC treatment or diagnosis.

papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a molecularly heterogeneous disease. This study aims to explore whether endocytosis pathway-associated genes and immune checkpoint-related features were linked to GC subtypes and prognosis. Public transcriptomic datasets from TCGA and GEO were analyzed. ssGSEA was applied to predefined endocytosis-related gene sets, and NMF was used to identify molecular subtypes. Survival, tumor microenvironment features, tumor mutation burden, microsatellite instability, and differentially expressed genes were evaluated. A three-gene prognostic model was developed and assessed through retrospective internal and external validation across public cohorts for prognostic association only. Two endocytosis-related subtypes were identified. The Group 1 subtype showed higher pathway activity, more immunosuppressive microenvironmental features, higher expression of selected immune checkpoint-related markers, and poorer survival. The Group 2 subtype showed lower pathway activity and more favorable outcomes. A three-gene signature (NRP1, SERPINE1, and MISP3) stratified patients into higher-risk and lower-risk groups across retrospective cohorts. Higher-risk cases were associated with worse overall survival and enrichment of epithelial-mesenchymal transition- and immune evasion-related pathways. This retrospective cross-cohort validation suggests that the prognostic signal was not restricted to a single dataset, but it does not demonstrate prospective clinical validity, analytical validity, or readiness for clinical implementation. Endocytosis-related molecular patterns may be associated with distinct biological and prognostic features in GC. The identified subtypes and prognostic signature should be interpreted as exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings that warrant further prospective, functional, and assay-level validation.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most commonly diagnosed malignancies among women worldwide and is frequently curable when identified at an early stage. However, advanced and metastatic disease continue to account for a substantial proportion of breast cancer-related deaths, particularly among patients with aggressive subtypes such as inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), a clinicopathologic entity that spans hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive, and triple-negative disease. Although advances in molecular profiling and systemic therapies have improved outcomes, substantial challenges persist in identifying patients at risk for recurrence, accurately assessing treatment response, and determining optimal therapeutic strategies. These challenges are driven by marked tumor heterogeneity and the dynamic interplay between malignant cells and their surrounding tumor microenvironment (TME). This review examines key barriers to the diagnosis and management of IBC, set against the broader landscape of advanced breast cancer. It discusses the clinical significance of late metastatic relapse, rapidly progressive disease, shortcomings of current prognostic frameworks, and the difficulties associated with monitoring metastatic involvement. Also highlighted are emerging approaches, including circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and other liquid biopsy technologies, that may enhance risk stratification, longitudinal surveillance, and detection of molecular resistance; these applications remain investigational, and established clinical approaches are distinguished from emerging strategies throughout. The TME is further explored as a critical determinant of tumor behavior, with emphasis on lymphoid and myeloid immune cells, stromal components, and immune checkpoint pathways that promote immune evasion and therapeutic resistance. Finally, this review surveys evolving treatment paradigms, including immunotherapeutic approaches, RNA-based diagnostics and therapeutics, most of which remain preclinical, and antibody-drug conjugates, which are expanding the therapeutic landscape for advanced disease. Together, these developments underscore the potential of integrating molecular, immunologic, and circulating biomarker data to enable more precise disease characterization and treatment selection, as essential for developing more effective, personalized strategies for patients with IBC and other advanced breast cancers.

papers.abstract: Accurate noninvasive estimation of pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) may support multidisciplinary discussions, but multimodal MRI-ultrasound evidence remains limited. We developed and externally validated a clinicopathological deep learning radiomics nomogram and explored its potential auxiliary value in a strictly hypothetical post-hoc surgical-planning scenario. With institutional review-board approval and waived consent, this retrospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study included 436 biopsy-proven TNBC patients who underwent NAT and surgery: Center 1 training cohort (n = 268) and internal validation cohort (n = 86), plus historical cases from cooperating Centers 2-3 for external validation (n = 82). pCR was defined as ypT0/is ypN0. Pretreatment dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)/apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and B-mode ultrasound were analyzed. Intratumoral and 5-mm peritumoral ring radiomics features were extracted and selected by LASSO. DenseNet-121 extracted modality-specific deep features, fused using multi-head self-attention. Age, tumor size, Ki-67, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), cT/N stage, and histological grade were integrated with imaging scores in a logistic-regression nomogram. Parameters and thresholds were locked after Center 1 development and applied once to external data. No model output was used clinically. Feature standardization and ComBat harmonization parameters were strictly locked to the training cohort before application to validation data. pCR occurred in 182/436 patients (41.7%). The nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.917 (95% CI, 0.881-0.947) in training, 0.883 (0.814-0.937) in internal validation, and 0.856 (0.773-0.921) in external validation, exceeding clinical (external AUC, 0.721), radiomics (0.786), and deep learning (0.819) models. External sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy at the locked threshold were 0.765, 0.813, and 0.793, respectively. Calibration was acceptable (slope, 0.93; intercept, -0.06; Brier score, 0.16). Decision curve analysis showed net benefit for thresholds of 0.20-0.70. Multi-threshold analysis revealed that a high-specificity threshold (0.65) yielded a positive predictive value of 0.85, potentially identifying a subset of patients with very high confidence of achieving pCR. Compared with the clinical model, external reclassification improved (continuous net reclassification improvement [NRI], 0.34; integrated discrimination improvement [IDI], 0.11; P = 0.003 and P = 0.008, respectively). Among the few multicenter TNBC studies combining MRI, ultrasound, intratumoral/peritumoral radiomics, and attention-based deep learning, this nomogram showed good retrospective accuracy for pCR prediction after NAT. The model is presented as an aid for pCR prediction and preoperative stratification rather than as direct support for surgical decision-making. Prospective validation and clinical-impact studies are required before implementation.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning framework that combines semi-automated segmentation, intratumoral habitats derived from multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), and multiscale peritumoral radiomics to predict high-grade prostate cancer (HGPCa) before surgery. This retrospective dual-center study involved 274 patients, comprising 208 from Center 1 for development and 66 from Center 2 for external test. The clinical and imaging variables included patient age, serum PSA, fPSA, PSAD, maximum tumor diameter, PI-RADS scores, and anatomical zone distribution (PZ vs. TZ). The development cohort was randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 145) and an internal validation cohort (n = 63). Intratumoral habitats were delineated using semi-automated segmentation and unsupervised K-means clustering, while peritumoral radiomic features were extracted from concentric 1-, 3-, and 5-mm shells. Predictive classifiers were optimized through machine learning algorithms, particularly a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for the habitat signature. A combined clinical-radiomics nomogram was constructed, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) employed to enhance model interpretability. Subgroup analyses were performed to assess the discriminative performance of the combined nomogram across the peripheral zone (PZ) and transition zone (TZ). The combined nomogram exhibited superior diagnostic performance, achieving AUCs of 0.914, 0.903, and 0.797 in the training cohort, internal validation cohort, and external test cohort, respectively. The MLP-based habitat model showed good discriminative performance, with AUCs of 0.896, 0.897, and 0.782 across the training cohort, internal validation cohort, and external test cohort, respectively. Among the peritumoral regions, the 5-mm shell demonstrated the best discriminative performance. SHAP analysis identified Habitat 1 Shape Sphericity as the most influential feature. Subgroup analysis demonstrated the discriminatory ability of the combined nomogram in both the PZ (AUC: 0.796) and TZ (AUC: 0.753) subgroups. The integration of semi-automated segmentation-based habitat analysis and peritumoral radiomics provides a promising approach for preoperative risk stratification of prostate cancer.

papers.abstract: Accurate preoperative risk stratification of cystic renal lesions (CRLs) remains a clinical challenge, primarily due to morphological overlap which often leads to the overtreatment of indolent cysts. To address this, we developed and validated an integrated deep learning framework that combines interactive segmentation with tri-phase CT feature integration to refine malignancy prediction. This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 434 patients with CRLs from four institutions, partitioned into training (n=195), validation (n=100), and external test (n=139) cohorts. The reference standard was histopathological diagnosis or ≥4 years of radiological stability. For volumetric segmentation, we implemented an interactive 'human-in-the-loop' Swin UNETR model. To integrate complementary information across the three CT phases, we then deployed a Tri-Phase-Channel (TPC) Perceiver architecture to integrate features extracted by parallel SEResNet50 backbones from unenhanced, corticomedullary, and nephrographic CT phases. Diagnostic performance was evaluated against the single-phase SEResNet50 models and the Bosniak classification version 2019 using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA). In the external test cohort, the interactive segmentation model yielded a Dice score of 0.890. For malignancy prediction, the TPC-Perceiver attained an AUC of 0.969 (95% CI: 0.911-1.000), significantly outperforming the Bosniak classification version 2019 (AUC 0.884; p =0.016). At the fixed probability threshold of 0.5, the model achieved a sensitivity of 94.4% and a specificity of 96.7%, compared with 100.0% and 76.9%, respectively, for the clinical standard. Furthermore, decision curve analysis indicated that the deep learning framework conferred greater net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. The integrated framework showed favorable performance for cystic renal lesion risk stratification. Exploratory pairwise AUC comparisons favored the TPC Perceiver over the single-phase models and the clinical Bosniak v2019 assessment, while its AUC was comparable to that of the previous SETD model. The sensitivity-specificity profile observed at the fixed threshold suggests potential value in reducing false-positive risk stratification. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, has attracted increasing attention in recent years because of its critical roles in tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune regulation. Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide and imposes a substantial mortality burden. This study aimed to systematically analyze the global research landscape, hotspots, and developmental trends of ferroptosis in CRC research from 2017 to 2025. English-language publications related to ferroptosis and CRC published between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2025, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus databases. A total of 1, 354 original articles and reviews were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the bibliometrix package in R were used for bibliometric and visualization analyses to evaluate annual publication trends, country/region and institutional collaboration networks, author contributions, journal distribution, co-cited references, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution. The number of publications in this field increased rapidly after 2020 and peaked in 2025. China ranked first in both publication output and total citations, followed by the United States, and China-United States collaboration constituted the core of the international collaboration network. Central South University was the most productive institution, while journals such as Frontiers in Oncology and Frontiers in Immunology served as major publication platforms. Research hotspots were mainly concentrated on chemotherapy resistance, the tumor immune microenvironment, PANoptosis, prognostic models, non-coding RNAs, gut microbiota, and the regulation of ferroptosis by traditional Chinese medicine and natural products. Ferroptosis has become a rapidly evolving frontier in CRC research. The research focus is gradually shifting from fundamental molecular mechanisms toward translational medical directions, including chemosensitization, combination immunotherapy, reversal of drug resistance, and precise prognostic evaluation. This study provides a systematic reference for understanding the global knowledge structure and future research directions in the field of ferroptosis and CRC.

papers.abstract: Uterine sarcomas represent a rare and heterogeneous group of malignancies whose management remains clinically challenging. They account for approximately 3%-5% of all uterine malignancies. Undifferentiated uterine sarcoma (UUS) is a subtype of uterine sarcomas. SMARCA4 is a tumor suppressor gene that is aberrantly altered in approximately 5%-7% of human malignancies. SMARCA4-deficient UUS is a highly aggressive, undifferentiated mesenchymal neoplasm associated with a median overall survival (OS) of 7 months. During tumorigenesis, loss of function of either SMARCA4 or SMARCA2 is frequently observed; however, concurrent loss of both genes has been reported to be synthetically lethal and is therefore considered unexpected. In this case report, a 52-year-old Chinese woman with early-stage UUS and SMARCA4 and SMARCA2 co-deficiency underwent surgical resection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and achieved a disease-free survival (DFS) of 32 months. This case suggests that patients with UUS harboring SMARCA4 and SMARCA2 co-deficiency may derive a survival benefit from early diagnosis and surgical resection. However, owing to the extreme rarity of UUS with co-deficiency of SMARCA4 and SMARCA2, conducting a high-level phase III randomized controlled trial to validate this observation remains impractical.

papers.abstract: The strategy for opportunistic endoscopic screening driven by family history of gastric cancer needs to be optimized in a tailored manner through further risk stratification. A hospital-based cross-sectional study included health check-up controls and gastric cancer patients at West China Hospital, Sichuan University. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, family history of malignancies, and serology were analyzed for associations with gastric cancer risk. Associations between family history of gastric cancer and incident gastric cancer risk were assessed, and a rapid cost-effectiveness analysis was performed. In total, 58,218 observations were analyzed, including 619 gastric cancer patients. Family history of gastric cancer was an independent risk factor for gastric cancer (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 5.59, 95% CI 3.81-8.20) and was associated with an increased risk of upper digestive tract benign comorbidities (aOR = 1.51, 95% CI 1.09-2.71). For persons with a family history of gastric cancer who were older than 40 years (odds ratio [OR] = 2.36, 95% CI 1.29-4.32), endoscopic screening could be mildly recommended in general practice. Endoscopic screening should be moderately recommended for those with a family history of gastric cancer if they were older than 60 years (OR = 8.90, 95% CI 3.84-20.61) and strongly recommended if they also had upper digestive tract benign comorbidities (OR = 16.78, 95% CI 7.03-40.06), seropositivity for carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and/or carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) (OR = 20.77, 95% CI 9.15-47.14), or anemia (OR = 80.11, 95% CI 33.07-194.05). A rapid cost-effectiveness analysis indicated that moderate-to-strong recommendations were preferred, but based on willingness-to-pay considerations, mild-to-strong recommendations had a considerable detection rate for gastric cancer. Sensitivity analysis yielded consistent findings for decision-making. Family history of gastric cancer is an independent risk factor for gastric cancer. Optimized risk stratification based on family history can improve the cost-effectiveness of detecting gastric cancer. The mechanism by which a family history of gastric cancer increases gastric cancer risk and a more tailored family history-driven endoscopic screening strategy require further investigation.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits profound molecular and metabolic heterogeneity associated with distinct phenotypic states. However, the contribution of transcription factor (TF)-driven regulatory programs to metabolic subtype stratification remains poorly understood. This study aims to determine whether TF-based classification can identify prognostically relevant glycolytic and lipogenic PDAC subtypes. Bulk transcriptomic data from multiple PDAC cohorts and single-cell RNA sequencing data were integrated to characterize TF-associated metabolic heterogeneity. Metabolic signatures and TFs were quantified using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) and AddModule Score (AMS). Differential expression, enrichment analysis, integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis, and deep neural network-based metabolic flux modeling were performed to investigate metabolic programs and functional differences between TF-defined subtypes. Additionally, RNA interference, RT-qPCR, lipid droplets staining, lactate assay, and transwell assays were used to evaluate the roles of TP63 in metabolic regulation. Glycolytic and lipogenic TF-defined metabolic subtypes were identified across multiple independent PDAC cohorts. These subtypes exhibited distinct metabolic programs, differentiation states, and prognostic outcomes. The glycolytic TF-defined subtype was associated with worse prognosis and differentiation, whereas the lipogenic TF-defined subtype exhibited more favorable clinical features. Integration of public bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses, together with deep neural network-based metabolic flux modeling, revealed consistent metabolic heterogeneity at both cellular and functional levels. Notably, TP63 was identified as a potential regulator of glycolytic-lipogenic metabolic reprogramming in PDAC. TF-based classification delineates glycolytic and lipogenic subtypes in PDAC, underscoring the critical role of TF-regulated metabolic programs in patient stratification. These findings highlight the prognostic significance of glycolytic and lipogenic metabolic heterogeneity and support the development of metabolism-targeted therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract: Cancer treatment-related oral mucositis (OM) is one of the most common adverse effects of cancer treatment and can substantially impair patients' quality of life. Its effective management depends heavily on patients' continuous self-management. This scoping review aimed to systematically map the intervention components, delivery modes, and existing limitations of self-management support interventions, thereby providing evidence to inform the optimization of intervention strategies. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews. Seven databases, including PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CINAHL, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and WanFang, were searched from inception to May 10, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data were charted using a standardized form and summarized using descriptive numerical and content analyses. A total of 7,132 records were identified, and 16 studies were ultimately included, comprising 9 quasi-experimental studies, 6 randomized controlled trials, and 1 mixed-methods study. The interventions were primarily hospital-based and nurse-led, with some incorporating digital tools or written materials. Reported outcomes generally included OM-related clinical outcomes, quality of life, self-management-related outcomes, and nutritional status, although the direction and magnitude of findings varied across studies. Existing studies have reported potential improvements in OM-related and self-management-related outcomes following self-management support interventions. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of heterogeneity in study designs, intervention components, and outcome measures, together with the absence of critical appraisal. Further well-designed studies using standardized outcome measures are needed to strengthen the evidence base.

papers.abstract: To determine whether heterogeneous genomic alterations detected by clinical tumor panels converge on a reproducible pathway-level difference between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and to examine its transcriptional output, cellular localization, and tumor-stromal coexpression context in public multi-omics cohorts. The institutional cohort comprised 52 patients who underwent tumor tissue genomic testing, including 28 with HCC and 24 in a CCA working cohort whose intrahepatic location was not uniformly documented. Ten canonical oncogenic pathways were compared using panel-aware evaluable denominators, and the selected pathway was tested in independent Memorial Sloan Kettering (MSK) cohorts. Matched genomic and transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were used to evaluate downstream pathway activity. GSE151530 and GSE189903 were analyzed by patient-level pseudobulk to localize the transcriptional difference, followed by CellChatDB-guided ligand-receptor coexpression analysis. Receptor tyrosine kinase-RAS (RTK-RAS) showed the strongest cancer-type difference in the institutional cohort: alterations were detected in 4/21 evaluable HCC cases and 8/11 evaluable CCA cases (odds ratio [OR] = 9.44; 95% CI, 1.87-47.70; P = 0.00601; Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted q = 0.0601), with concordant directions across sensitivity analyses. In MSK, integrated RTK-RAS alterations occurred in 240/412 intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) cases (58.3%) and 107/289 HCC cases (37.0%; OR = 2.37; 95% CI, 1.74-3.22; P = 3.12 × 10-8). In TCGA, RTK-RAS status was associated with higher mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) activity in the pooled cancer-type-adjusted model (β = 0.240; 95% CI, 0.051-0.428; P = 0.0129), whereas the within-iCCA estimate was positive but imprecise. Patient-level single-cell meta-analysis localized the higher iCCA MAPK activity predominantly to malignant cells (pooled effect = 1.455; 95% CI, 0.658-2.252; P = 3.46 × 10-4; q = 0.00208). Platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF)-PDGFRA and insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-IGF1R coexpression patterns accompanied this malignant-cell phenotype. Panel-aware integration of clinical genomic testing and public multi-omics data supports a higher burden of heterogeneous RTK-RAS alterations in CCA/iCCA than in HCC and links this difference to a malignant-cell MAPK transcriptional phenotype. The pathway-level framework complements, rather than replaces, established alteration-specific interpretation and generates tumor-stromal coexpression hypotheses for further spatial and functional testing.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to provide new insights into systemic treatment for BRAF wild-type metastatic unresectable melanoma, thereby offering a basis for personalized clinical decision-making. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible participants were adults with pathologically confirmed BRAF V600 wild-type metastatic unresectable melanoma. Outcomes included progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Network meta-analysis (NMA) results were presented as league tables and the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values. In total, 8 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 3,418 patients and 9 systemic treatment strategies were included. One open-label study was rated as having some concerns, while the remaining seven were rated as low risk of bias across all domains and overall. The NMA results showed that, compared to ipilimumab, pembrolizumab, nivolumab, nivolumab + relatlimab, and nivolumab + ipilimumab demonstrated significant advantages in improving OS. Notably, nivolumab + relatlimab ranked first in prolonging OS (SUCRA = 93.94%). In the PFS analysis, this regimen had the highest SUCRA value only within the connected network consisting of dacarbazine, nivolumab, and the combination of nivolumab and relatlimab (SUCRA = 98.86%), although no comparisons or standardized rankings were performed between different PFS networks. The results of OS primary analysis for nivolumab plus relatlimab, as well as its ranking within the corresponding PFS network, are exploratory in nature. They are intended solely to generate research hypotheses and should not be interpreted as evidence of superiority over other treatments or as a basis for changing the current standard of care. Direct head-to-head RCTs are still needed to further clarify the comparative efficacy of the relevant regimens.

papers.abstract: Malignant ascites is a common, severe complication of advanced solid tumors, driven by multifactorial pathogenesis, including impaired lymphatic drainage, vascular endothelial growth factor-induced vascular hyperpermeability, pro-permeability inflammatory cytokines, and profound peritoneal immunosuppression. Clinically, it correlates with poor prognosis, reduced overall survival, and substantial quality-of-life deterioration. Current treatment remains predominantly palliative: repeated large-volume paracentesis offers transient symptom relief, fails to prevent reaccumulation, and carries procedural risks. Emerging evidence indicates malignant ascites is not merely passive fluid accumulation but an active, immunosuppressive niche shaped by bidirectional crosstalk among tumor cells, stromal components, diverse immune subsets (e.g., regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, dysfunctional CD8+ T cells), and soluble mediators. This narrative review summarizes recent advances in immunomodulatory treatment for malignant ascites, with an emphasis on strategies targeting the ascitic immune microenvironment. Intraperitoneal administration of immune checkpoint inhibitors has shown acceptable safety and preliminary activity in early-phase single-arm trials, although confirmatory data from larger controlled studies are lacking. In randomized trials, the T-cell engager catumaxomab prolonged puncture-free survival, while the bispecific antibody M701 has shown similar benefits in a phase II randomized controlled study; these findings support further investigation of localized T-cell redirection. Preclinical and early-phase clinical studies suggest that intraperitoneal oncolytic viruses can induce immunogenic tumor cell death and T-cell activation, with single-cell analyses indicating remodeling of the ascitic immune microenvironment. Future directions include integrating ascites immune phenotyping, patient-derived organoids for drug sensitivity testing, and machine learning-based decision support to guide personalized immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Scientific satire occupies an unusual place in medical publishing. This editorial discusses the role of medical satire by highlighting an article that poses as a retrospective observational trial using a large database, and compares a clinically relevant outcome between two arbitrary, physiologically meaningless groups. The differences between the groups are statistically significant, but physiologically nonsensical. The editorial explores epistemology as it applies to the practice of medicine. The greatest value of the satire may be medical education and its teaching of clinical reasoning. It reminds clinicians that cognitive heuristics, arbitrary categorisation, and large datasets can combine to produce statistically convincing, yet clinically meaningless, associations.

papers.abstract: Importance Metabolic syndrome (MetS) includes obesity, insulin resistance, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. While androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is associated with an increased risk of dyslipidemia, adiposity, and MetS, evidence is limited on the occurrence and timing of metabolic dysfunction among men receiving concurrent androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) therapy and whether patterns vary by age. Objective To characterize the occurrence and rate of MetS during the first year following initiation of ADT-ARPI, examine associations with age and ARPI type, and evaluate component metabolic outcomes (secondary end points). Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study of adult patients from January 2014 to September 2025 with up to 12 months of follow-up per person used data from a national, deidentified health record dataset (Epic Cosmos) and included patients with prostate cancer who initiated treatment with ADT-ARPI (abiraterone acetate, enzalutamide, apalutamide, and darolutamide) without evidence of MetS or its components before treatment. Data were analyzed between October 2025 and January 2026 (further analyses were done with revisions through May 2026). Exposure Concurrent ADT and ARPI use, with index date defined as the first date of overlap between therapies. Main Outcomes and Measures New-onset MetS during the 12 months following the index date. Secondary outcomes included individual metabolic abnormalities. Results The cohort included 16 924 men with prostate cancer (mean [SD] age, 73.1 [9.1] y; 509 [3.0%] Asian individuals, 912 [5.4%] Hispanic individuals, 3562 [21.0%] non-Hispanic Black individuals, and 11 083 [65.5%] non-Hispanic White individuals). Medical ADT use predominated, and enzalutamide was the most frequently used ARPI. During the first year following initiation of concurrent ADT and ARPI therapy, the cumulative incidence of metabolic syndrome increased steadily, reaching nearly 40%, and varied by age group. Hypertension was the most frequently documented component outcome. Metabolic associations varied by age, with the highest incidence of metabolic syndrome among patients aged 70 to 79 years (51.7 events per 1000 person-months; 95% CI, 50.7-53.9). Heterogeneity in metabolic outcomes by ARPI type was observed in exploratory analyses. Conclusions and Relevance This study found that while ARPIs are standard of care for advanced prostate cancer, metabolic abnormalities were frequently documented shortly after initiation of concurrent ADT and ARPI therapy. This suggests that monitoring should extend beyond cancer-specific outcomes to include early detection of metabolic dysfunction, ideally through multidisciplinary care. The early burden of metabolic abnormalities highlights the need to evaluate scalable interventions addressing cardiometabolic risk in men with prostate cancer.

papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence has high potential for impact in healthcare applications, but its training and deployment are challenging due to diverse data, a complex spectrum of possible tasks and important privacy needs. High-performing foundation models that enable data-efficient fine-tuning for diverse downstream tasks can meaningfully accelerate development in this domain. We introduce MedGemma, a collection of medical vision-language foundation models based on Gemma 3. MedGemma demonstrates advanced medical understanding and reasoning across images and text and multiple medical imaging domains, exceeding the performance of similarly sized generative models while maintaining the general capabilities of the Gemma base models. For out-of-distribution tasks, MedGemma achieves improvements of 2.6–10% in medical image question answering, 15.5–18.1% in chest X-ray finding classification and 10.8% in agentic evaluations compared with the base models. Our results show that fine-tuning MedGemma can be more effective than fine-tuning the base Gemma 3 model for medical tasks, particularly in the setting of limited training data. We additionally introduce MedSigLIP, a medically tuned vision encoder derived from SigLIP. MedSigLIP powers the visual understanding capabilities of MedGemma and, as an encoder, achieves performance comparable to or better than that of many specialized medical image encoders. Taken together, the MedGemma collection provides a strong foundation of medical image and text capabilities, with the potential to accelerate medical research and the development of downstream applications.

papers.abstract: Abstract The Tn antigen, a truncated O-glycan, is frequently elevated in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Multiple therapeutic approaches targeting Tn have been developed, but they have not demonstrated clear efficacy signals in early-phase clinical studies. Improving Tn-targeted strategies in PDAC will require both overcoming the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and defining pathways by which truncated O-glycans promote growth and immune evasion. In this study, we show that Tn reshapes the tumor immune landscape of PDAC. Expression of Tn antigen on PDAC cells enhanced proliferation in vitro and tumor growth in vivo. Tn expression remodeled the immune microenvironment, skewing tumor-associated macrophages toward M2-like phenotypes, reducing cross-presenting dendritic cells, and expanding myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC). Single-cell RNA sequencing confirmed the expansion of MDSCs and downregulation of antigen processing and presentation in the immune cell infiltrate of Tn+ tumors. Tumor-intrinsic transcriptomic analyses revealed the activation of TNFα/NF-κB signaling and induction of IL34, a cytokine linked to monocyte survival and differentiation in Tn antigen–expressing tumors. Additionally, high Tn expression in both organoids derived from patients with pancreatic cancer and in PDAC mouse models was associated with increased IL34 expression. The genetic deletion of Il34 in PDAC cells attenuated Tn-driven tumorigenesis and reduced MDSC infiltration, whereas recombinant IL34 promoted myeloid cell differentiation and proliferation in vitro. Together, these findings establish a glyco–immune–cytokine axis in which truncated O-glycans contribute to IL34-mediated immunosuppression, providing mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets in PDAC. Significance: Altered glycosylation stimulates TNF-α/NF-κB signaling and induces IL-34-mediated accumulation of suppressive myeloid cells in pancreatic cancer, providing a myeloid-mediated mechanism of immunosuppression that could guide the development of therapies targeting glycosylation.

papers.abstract: Background: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) is the second most common primary liver cancer. Macrophages are crucial components of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2-positive (TREM2 + ) macrophages have recently emerged as potent pro-tumor progress players in several cancers. However, the heterogeneity and tumor-promoting mechanisms of macrophages especially TREM2 + macrophages in ICC remain systematically unexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to systematically elucidate the heterogeneity of macrophages in ICC, with a specific focus on the pro-tumor role of TREM2 + macrophages. Methods: We collected tumor tissues, adjacent nontumor tissues, and tumor-adjacent border tissues from 16 ICC patients. These samples were subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic sequencing, followed by comprehensive analysis. The findings were further validated through flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, multiplex immunofluorescence, and in vitro cellular assays. Furthermore, we established an ICC model using genetically engineered ( Trem2 −/− ) mice as a validation cohort to corroborate the discoveries from human samples. Results: Macrophages are important prognostic factors in ICC, with functional heterogeneity. TREM2 + macrophages in tumor tissues promote immune suppression by exhausting CD8 + T cells and inducing the generation of regulatory T cells to produce. At the tumor border region, TREM2 + macrophages enhance ICC invasion via the urokinase-type plasminogen activator–urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor axis and induce hepatic stellate cell conversion to myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblast, forming a physical immune barrier that impedes CD8 + T cell infiltration in tumor tissues. TIMD4 + macrophages in adjacent tissues also suppress CD8 + T cell function. Combining anti-Trem2 and anti-Timd4 with anti-Pd-1 antibodies significantly improved treatment outcomes in the ICC mice. Conclusions: TREM2 + and TIMD4 + macrophages are key regulators of the immunosuppressive TME in ICC. Targeting Trem2 and Timd4 enhances the effectiveness of anti-Pd-1 therapy in ICC mouse models.

papers.abstract: Background: Bacteria-mediated cancer therapy is emerging as a promising approach due to its low cost, scalability, and sustained efficacy. While bacterial immunomodulation has been extensively studied, the role of bacterial metabolic competition, particularly for glucose, in tumor suppression remains unclear. We aimed to investigate how engineered Salmonella strains exploit metabolic competition to trigger antitumor immunity and improve therapeutic outcomes in bladder cancer models. Methods: Using genetic screening, we generated a gluconeogenesis-deficient Salmonella strain, the AISIH strain with the glpX gene knocked out (GLA1), with enhanced glucose uptake. In vitro and in vivo assays were performed to assess tumor cell glucose deprivation, mitochondrial stress, cytosolic mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release, and activation of the cGAS/STING pathway. An engineered strain, GLA2, was generated from the AISIH strain by knockout of the glpX gene and was subsequently further engineered to locally deliver an anti-tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) nanobody under quorum-sensing control. Efficacy was evaluated in subcutaneous and orthotopic bladder cancer models, with analysis of tumor-infiltrating immune cells, dendritic cell (DC) maturation, and T cell priming. Results: GLA1 competitively depleted glucose in the bladder tumor microenvironment, inducing energy stress, mitochondrial damage, and mtDNA release, which noncanonically activated the STING pathway. This promoted type I interferon production, DC maturation, and antitumor immune responses. However, TNF-α-mediated vascular abnormalities limited efficacy. GLA2 normalized tumor vasculature via local anti-TNF-α delivery, enhancing nutrient competition and immune activation. Both strains markedly suppressed tumor growth, with GLA2 showing superior efficacy due to synergistic metabolic and immune reprogramming. Conclusions: This study demonstrates that bacterial competition for glucose is a pivotal mechanism of antitumor activity in bladder cancer, linking metabolic stress to STING-dependent immune activation. Engineered Salmonella strains that combine enhanced glucose uptake with local vascular normalization offer a robust platform for bladder cancer. These findings highlight a novel strategy to integrate microbial metabolic engineering with immune modulation, providing a foundation for precision bacteriotherapy in oncology.

papers.abstract: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is driven by the constitutively active BCR::ABL1 kinase, which promotes uncontrolled cell proliferation. Although protein-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have revolutionized CML treatment, resistance remains a significant barrier to curative therapy, particularly due to BCR::ABL1 mutations and the persistence of leukemia stem cells (LSCs). New treatment strategies that directly inhibit BCR::ABL1 protein expression are needed to achieve more effective therapy. Using a high-content antibody microarray and bioinformatics analyses, we investigated differences in the proteome and phosphorylation landscape of Imatinib (IM)-resistant cells and identified highly activated members of the eukaryotic translation initiation complex (eIF4F), particularly eIF4G1, a core component of eIF4F. These eIF4F complex members are highly expressed and activated in CD34+ CML stem/progenitor cells and in IM-resistant cells. Genetic inhibition of eIF4G1 or pharmacological targeting with the small-molecule inhibitor SBI-756 diminished eIF4F complex assembly, reduced overall translation initiation, reduced BCR::ABL1 expression and key downstream targets, impaired the survival of nonresponder stem/progenitor cells, including BCR::ABL1-T315I mutant cells, and sensitized them to TKIs, with strong synergistic effects in vitro and in a PDX model. These findings underscore the potential of eIF4F complex inhibition as a new therapeutic strategy to overcome TKI resistance in CML and other BCR::ABL1+ malignancies.

papers.abstract: In Head and Neck Cancer (HNC), even short delays in treatment can worsen prognosis. We used real-world data to quantify waiting times and identify patient, tumour and health service factors associated with treatment delay in England. Using linked national datasets (Cancer Registry, Cancer Waiting Times, Hospital Episodes Statistics, Radiotherapy and Chemotherapy), we calculated waiting times from referral to first treatment (surgery or (chemo)radiation) and used multivariable logistic regression models to examine factors associated with delay. Of 30,506 patients, 43% experienced treatment delay ( > 62 days from referral). Long delays ( > 90 days) affected 11% of patients treated with primary surgery and 20% of those receiving primary (chemo)radiation. Non-urgent referral (30% of patients) was the strongest predictor of long delay (aOR 4.07, CI: 3.54-4.68). Additional risk-factors included initial assessment at non-specialist (spoke) hospitals, non-oropharyngeal cancers, and higher socio-economic deprivation. Treatment delays in HNC are worsening, particularly for patients treated with primary (chemo)radiation. Referral route is the strongest determinant. Interventions should focus on optimising referral pathways, increasing awareness of HNC symptoms among the public and primary care, and acknowledging the different drivers of delay associated with surgery and (chemo)radiation therapy.

papers.abstract: Evaluation of arterial resection (AR) during pancreatoduodenectomy (PD) remains limited. This study compares PD with AR to PD with venous resection (VR) and no vascular resection (NVR). Patient demographics, outcomes, and changes over 5 years are evaluated. In this study, NSQIP data was analyzed comparing patients undergoing PD with AR to NVR and VR. Demographics and 30-day post-operative outcomes were compared, and multivariable modeling evaluated factors associated with serious complications and mortality. Propensity score matched (PSM) analysis compared AR to NVR, AR to VR, and VR to NVR. We evaluated 28,083 patients with 4.1% having AR and 10.9% having VR. After demographic adjustment, both AR (1.40; p < 0.001) and VR (OR 1.32; p < 0.001) were independently associated with serious complications and mortality (AR: OR 2.03; p = 0.002; VR: OR 1.43; p = 0.043). PSM supported increased serious complications (+4.9% VR, p < 0.001; +5.40% AR, p = 0.008) but not mortality (+0.4% VR, p = 0.323; +1.4% AR, p = 0.067) compared to NVR. AR did not increase the risk of complications or mortality compared to VR following PSM. Evaluating AR/VR from 2017 to 2021 shows consistent demographics but increasing neoadjuvant treatment (40.2%-48.9%; p < 0.001). Length of stay has decreased (12.3-9.6 days; p < 0.001), while serious complications (19.7%-22.1%) and mortality (1.7%-3.1%) remained similar. Results demonstrate that arterial (and venous) resection during PD is independently associated with 30-day serious complications compared to without vascular resection. However, absolute morbidity rates during vascular resection may be acceptable in selected patients and appear to be similar with arterial and venous resection. Future studies evaluating long-term outcomes are needed.

papers.abstract: BRCAness, a phenotype associated with homologous recombination deficiency, has not been fully characterized in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), especially regarding prognosis and regimen-specific postoperative management. We analyzed 137 patients with TNBC who had residual invasive disease after NAC. BRCAness status was assessed in surgical specimens using multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA). Its associations with clinicopathological features and survival were evaluated according to NAC regimen, and prognostic models for disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) were developed by combining BRCAness with clinicopathological variables. BRCAness was identified in 42.3% of tumors and was associated with high histological grade, high Ki-67, and perineural invasion. Patients with BRCAness-positive tumors had worse survival than those with BRCAness-negative tumors (5-year DFS, 50.0% vs. 68.2%, p = 0.020; 5-year OS, 58.6% vs. 78.1%, p = 0.014). This prognostic effect was evident in patients treated with anthracycline-based NAC, but not in those treated with platinum-based regimens. Models incorporating BRCAness showed good discrimination (DFS C-index, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.62-0.78; OS C-index, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.69-0.81). Among BRCAness-positive patients who had received anthracycline-based NAC, adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with better survival (5-year DFS, 55.6% vs. 27.3%, p = 0.035; 5-year OS, 66.7% vs. 36.4%, p = 0.023). BRCAness was associated with poorer outcome in residual TNBC after NAC and may help identify patients with different prognoses and postoperative treatment patterns.

papers.abstract: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection in a subset of cases. We previously showed that the incidence of HL in Taiwan increased ~2.5-fold between 2001 and 2020, particularly among young women with the nodular sclerosis (NS) subtype. In this nationwide multicenter study, we evaluated EBV status in HL to determine its impact on clinicopathologic features and survival outcomes. We found that the proportion of EBV-associated HL in Taiwan declined over the past two decades, from 39% to 27%. EBV-positive frequency exhibited a bimodal age distribution, peaking in children 70 years (80%), with the lowest frequency in patients 20-29 years (11%). Compared with EBV-negative patients, EBV-positive patients were older (53.5 vs. 32.9 years; p 60 years), B symptoms, non-NS histology, EBV-positivity, advanced-stage disease (Stage III-IV), and a high International Prognostic Score (IPS, 4-7). On multivariate analysis, older age and a high IPS retained prognostic significance. Large registry datasets from Taiwan and the US further demonstrated that survival outcomes have improved over the past two decades. Female patients and those with the NS and nodular lymphocyte-predominant subtypes had significantly better survival. These findings provide insight into the biological impact of EBV in HL and help inform strategies for disease prevention and management.

papers.abstract: Since the discovery and application of green fluorescent protein for use as an optical tag, fluorescent proteins (FPs) have changed the way we observe biological signals and processes. FP and fluorescent biosensor design has continued to advance, facilitated by new technologies and developments in chemistry, physics, engineering and screening technologies. We summarize some of the recent developments in FP engineering, focusing on insights that have led to improved photostability or longer wavelengths, among other improvements, highlighting mScarlet as a case study. We also discuss the engineering of new fluorescent biosensors, focusing on the ways in which screening, quantitative imaging, spatial resolution and multiplexing have been improved in recent years. Finally, we conclude with a perspective on what the future holds for the next generation of FPs and biosensors.

papers.abstract: The parent body of the C-type asteroid Ryugu experienced aqueous alteration. The past aqueous environments have been reconstructed using mineralogies and geochemical modeling, often assuming Na-Cl-rich fluid compositions. Here, we reconstruct Ryugu's aqueous environment using chemical equilibrium modeling constrained by Electron Probe Microanalyzer (EPMA) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy. Our results suggest that Ryugu water possessed lower salinity than previously estimated and was highly reducing (Eh: -0.5 to -0.8 V) and strongly alkaline (pH: 10.3 to 11.5) conditions conducive to prebiotic organic reactions. The inferred high hydrogen fugacity, lack of NaCl, and low salinity recorded in Ryugu sample suggest that aqueous alteration occurred beneath a surface ice layer, with subsequent ice sublimation driving water loss. These findings refine our understanding of C-type asteroids evolution and the quantity and nature of water delivered to the early Earth.

papers.abstract: Our understanding of cell division control traditionally comes via using liquid broths or 2D flat-plate cultures - which cannot recapitulate the complex visco-elasto-plastic properties of natural habitats such as tissues, mucus, and soil. Consequently, how such regimes of physical confinement influence proliferative growth remains poorly understood. Here, using engineered, mechanically tunable and transparent growth matrices, we directly visualize yeast budding and division across 3D viscoelastic regimes. We discover that elevated physical confinement drastically prolongs budding intervals without any physiological defects or activating global regulatory programs. Remarkably, extended cell division times are not associated with transcriptional or proteomic signatures of mechanosensation or cell cycle regulation. Rather, 3D confinement physically constrains the volumetric growth of incipient buds - manifesting as delayed cell cycle progression. Hence, our findings establish that physical constrainment regulates eukaryotic cell division.

papers.abstract: Despite significant climate variability in the Northern Hemisphere ~50,000-12,000 years ago, the potential for vertebrates to periodically thrive in the glacial Arctic Ocean has been largely overlooked because ecosystem productivity was assumed to be too low. Here, we analyze fish otoliths preserved in deep-sea sediments and find that two Arctic endemic cod species, ice cod (Arctogadus glacialis) and polar cod (Boreogadus saida), lived at 87-89 °N ~ 48,000-35,000 years ago and reappeared at the onset of the Holocene ~12,000 years ago. A. glacialis also occurred north of Greenland at 84-85 °N ~ 20,000 years ago, during the peak of the Last Glacial Maximum, suggesting the presence of refugia that enabled survival and divergence from B. saida under the harshest climate conditions. These findings suggest that the glacial Arctic Ocean was not a barren ice desert but rather a breeding ground for the evolution of cold adaptation in marine fish.

papers.abstract: Understanding the functional consequences of genetic variants, particularly those classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), is a major challenge in genomics. While variant effects at protein level are well recognized, roles in post-transcriptional regulation are increasingly appreciated. Here, we introduce cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout), a scalable method for assessing variant effects at RNA level. cPRIME employs prime editing to insert genetic variants into endogenous genomic loci, followed by the quantification of changes in variant frequencies at RNA (cDNA) and genomic DNA (gDNA) level. We demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse karyotypes and genomic loci and reveal that synonymous marker edits - frequently used in prime editing screens - can themselves alter RNA processing and thereby confound the interpretation of variant effects. Taken together, cPRIME provides a platform for studying the post-transcriptional consequences of genetic variants in their genomic context and establishes a framework for the functional interpretation of RNA-altering variants in cancer and other diseases.

papers.abstract: Intensive care unit-acquired pneumonia is often treated as a binary diagnosis, although clinical deterioration, imaging and microbial detection describe different aspects of disease. This Perspective proposes an explicit, graded and revisable assessment of whether a detected organism plausibly causes the current lung injury. The framework encompasses pneumonia arising during ventilation, pneumonia that precedes intubation and pneumonia in non-ventilated ICU patients. It places molecular results within clinical, anatomical, microbiological and host context and uses formal reassessment at 48-72 hours to guide treatment continuation, narrowing or discontinuation.

papers.abstract: To assess whether the association between postoperative diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and neurological worsening after eloquent-area glioma surgery differs according to lesion morphology. We retrospectively analyzed 139 consecutive patients undergoing resection of eloquent-area supratentorial gliomas (WHO 2-4). Postoperative MRI (< 48 h) classified lesions as sector- or rim-shaped. Neurological status was assessed at discharge and 4-6 months. DWI lesions occurred in 44/139 patients (31.7%; 31 sector-shaped, 13 rim-shaped); 59 (42.4%) worsened at discharge. Overall, DWI positivity alone was not associated with worsening. Sector-shaped DWI lesions were associated with neurological worsening (positive predictive value, PPV of 58.1%) and remained associated after multivariable adjustment (OR 3.83, 95% CI 1.30-11.29), although the confidence interval was wide and the unadjusted association was borderline. Rim-shaped lesions carried a PPV of 38.5%, comparable to the risk in DWI-negative patients (37.9%), and the two morphologies did not differ significantly in direct comparison. Awake craniotomy was also independently associated with worsening, and frontal site with a lower risk. 61% of worsening occurred with negative DWI. A deficit was present at the 4-6 month follow-up in 9 patients (6.5%), all with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, and was associated with a ≥ 50% evoked-potential decrease. In this cohort, postoperative DWI positivity was associated with neurological worsening mainly when the lesion was sector-shaped, a finding that requires confirmation in larger series. Rim-shaped lesions showed a risk of worsening similar to that of a negative scan. Most worsening occurs without DWI ischemia, suggesting non-ischemic mechanisms of function-guided surgery. A deficit at follow-up occurred only in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and was associated with intraoperative neurophysiological changes.

papers.abstract: Missed genetic deletions can prevent cancer patients from receiving effective targeted therapy. Standard pipelines, such as TSO500, use bin count averaging for copy number variation detection but often overlook focal events. To address this, we developed a machine learning (ML) pipeline for deletion detection and zygosity evaluation within the MASTERsg precision oncology program. We focused on the tumor suppressor gene PTEN, whose loss confers sensitivity to mTOR/Akt inhibition. An Extreme Gradient Boosting model trained on PTEN-deleted and wild-type tumor samples identified focal deletions missed by the TSO500 pipeline and CNVkit that were associated with concordant PTEN protein loss by immunohistochemistry. Importantly, the model detected PTEN deletions in 33/204 profiled samples that were classified as PTEN wild-type by TSO500; 75% (15/20) of stainable cases showed absent or reduced PTEN protein expression. These findings demonstrate the potential of ML to enhance panel sequencing, uncovering therapeutically relevant alterations missed by established diagnostic methods.

papers.abstract: Therapeutic efficacy of temozolomide (TMZ) remains limited, and GBM patients generally experience poor outcomes due to the presence of multiple mechanisms of TMZ resistance. Previously, we developed two novel compounds: EPIC-1027, which targets HOTAIR/PRC2 complex, and EPIC-1042, which disrupts interaction between PTRF and CAV1. In this study, we aim to establish a novel combinatorial strategy for GBM by targeting mitochondrial function. Proteomics was employed to evaluate global protein alterations induced by EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042. Super-resolution microscopy and transmission electron microscopy were used to characterize changes in mitochondrial morphology. Metabolic flux analysis was performed to assess alterations in cellular energy metabolism following combined treatment. An intracranial GBM model was established to validate the anti-GBM efficacy of EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 in vivo. Combined treatment with EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 reduced the abundance of respiratory chain complex proteins by promoting p62-dependent protein degradation, resulting in severe mitochondrial damage. Both glycolytic activity and oxidative phosphorylation were markedly suppressed following EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 treatment. In vitro, EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 exerted a synergistic inhibitory effect on GBM cell proliferation and significantly induced apoptosis in an MGMT-independent manner. In vivo, combined treatment with EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 significantly attenuated tumor growth and prolonged survival in mice bearing orthotopic GBM. Our study demonstrates that combined treatment with EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 induces mitochondrial structural abnormalities and functional impairment, leading to suppressed proliferation and enhanced apoptosis. These findings identified a novel combinatorial therapeutic strategy targeting mitochondria for the treatment of glioblastoma.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy has achieved clinical progress in various malignancies, yet primary and acquired resistance limits its efficacy in solid tumors. Myeloid cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME), including tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs), and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), undergo metabolic reprogramming under hypoxia and nutrient stress. They impair effector T cell function and may contribute to exhaustion-associated states via nutrient competition, release of toxic metabolites, and formation of physical barriers, representing a critical resistance mechanism. This review summarizes the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of myeloid cells and the metabolic networks underlying their immunosuppressive phenotypes, focusing on dysregulated lipid and cholesterol metabolism, amino acid remodeling, the glycolytic switch, and subcellular stress responses. We analyze how metabolic dysregulation causes T cell dysfunction and, in defined contexts, contributes to exhaustion-associated transcriptional programs through nutrient competition, toxic metabolite accumulation, and upregulation of inhibitory receptor ligands, and summarize intervention strategies targeting myeloid recruitment, phenotypic remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and pathological structures combined with ICB. We discuss challenges of efficacy heterogeneity and safety in clinical translation, and highlight the prospects of multi-omics and computational biology in guiding next-generation combination immunotherapy. Understanding myeloid metabolic plasticity may provide a basis for overcoming immunotherapy resistance and establishing precise synergistic strategies.

papers.abstract: Persistent CAR-T donor cells after CAR-T-bridged allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) may complicate hematopoietic recovery. When CAR-T and HSCT cells share the same donor, standard donor chimerism cannot distinguish their contributions. We report three patients with relapsed/refractory T-cell malignancies who received CAR-T and allo-HSCT from distinct donors, enabling three-party short tandem repeat (STR) analysis to resolve CAR-T donor, HSCT donor, and recipient compartments. Patient 2, with detectable residual CAR transgene at transplantation (240 copies/µg gDNA), developed mixed chimerism with cytopenia (MCC) and a CAR-T donor contribution of 47.72%. Patient 3, also with detectable residual CAR transgene (22,162 copies/µg gDNA), developed mixed chimerism, with a CAR-T donor contribution of 14.23%. In contrast, Patient 1, with undetectable CAR transgene at transplantation, showed stable complete donor chimerism (CDC) and hematopoietic recovery. Guided by the two-step reconstitution pattern observed in Patient 1, we administered CAR-target-knockout donor lymphocyte infusion (KO-DLI) as rescue treatment in Patient 2 and preemptive intervention in Patient 3. Both eventually became CAR-undetectable, with restoration of CDC and hematologic recovery, although the independent effect of KO-DLI could not be isolated. All three remain in complete remission (follow-up + 713, +335, + 201 days). Residual CAR transgene at transplantation may serve as an early risk signal for CAR-T donor cell persistence, and KO-DLI warrants prospective validation as a transplantation-sparing salvage approach.

papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of tumor progression and immune suppression within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Emerging evidence identifies ubiquitination, a dynamic post-translational modification that regulates protein stability, localization, and signaling activity, as a critical determinant of TAM function. Ubiquitin signaling orchestrates macrophage inflammatory responses, metabolic reprogramming, and tumor cell-immune cell crosstalk through coordinated actions of ubiquitin-activating enzymes, ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes, ubiquitin-protein ligases (E3s), and deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs). Dysregulation of these ubiquitin networks fosters an immunosuppressive microenvironment, thereby promoting tumor growth, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the role of ubiquitination in TAM biology, focusing on key E3 ubiquitin ligases and DUBs in TAM immunity. We further discuss emerging ubiquitin-dependent signaling pathways that integrate metabolic and inflammatory cues within TAMs. Finally, we highlight the therapeutic potential of targeting ubiquitination machinery to reprogram TAMs and remodel the TME. Collectively, this review provides a comprehensive framework for understanding ubiquitin-mediated regulation of TAM function and offers novel perspectives for developing ubiquitination-based cancer immunotherapies.

papers.abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) of histone H3 at lysine 9 (H3K9) contribute to chromatin homeostasis and transcriptional regulation and have been implicated in cancer progression. However, how distinct H3K9 modification states differ in function, compete for the same lysine residue, and dynamically respond to cellular context remains incompletely understood. This review summarizes the biochemical characteristics and enzymatic regulation of H3K9 methylation, acetylation, and non-acetyl acylations, including lactylation, β-hydroxybutyrylation, butyrylation, and crotonylation. We examine their roles in DNA replication, transcription, and DNA damage repair, as well as their interplay with other epigenetic regulatory mechanisms. We further discuss how H3K9-associated regulatory networks contribute to tumor proliferation, stemness maintenance, metabolic reprogramming, invasion and metastasis, immune microenvironment remodeling, therapeutic resistance, and programmed cell death, emphasizing their context-dependent and, in some settings, opposing biological effects. Finally, we evaluate preclinical and clinical advances in pharmacologically targeting H3K9-associated regulatory enzymes, distinguishing residue-specific mechanistic evidence from broader enzyme-level effects, and outline future directions for biomarker-guided epigenetic therapies in cancer.

papers.abstract: The intratumoral microbiome critically influences immunotherapy efficacy by modulating the host immune microenvironment and epigenetic landscape through its metabolites. Microbial derived metabolites such as short chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, trimethylamine N oxide, and tryptophan derivatives reprogram host cell epigenetics via DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNAs, thereby shaping anti-tumor immunity and driving either immune activation or resistance. In turn, the hypoxic, acidic, and nutrient deprived tumor microenvironment reshapes microbial composition and metabolism, forming a vicious cycle that further affects therapeutic outcomes. Given these pivotal roles, targeting the intratumoral microbiota has emerged as a promising strategy. Advances in synthetic biology have enabled the development of engineered bacteria as programmable living therapeutics. These engineered strains achieve tumor specific colonization, controlled drug release, and multimodal functions such as cytokine secretion, immune checkpoint blockade, STING pathway activation, and metabolic reprogramming. By enhancing immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy and synergizing with cell therapies, engineered bacterial therapy represents a highly promising approach to improve immunotherapy efficiency. Despite challenges in clinical translation including heterogeneity, anti-vector immunity, and manufacturing complexity, this strategy offers a new paradigm for precision cancer treatment.

papers.abstract: AXL is a membrane-accessible receptor tyrosine kinase and a potential antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) target, but its therapeutic relevance in soft-tissue sarcoma remains incompletely defined. We evaluated the AXL-directed pyrrolobenzodiazepine ADC ADCT-601/mipasetamab uzoptirine using a sarcoma tissue microarray, patient-derived cell lines, and patient-derived xenografts. AXL expression was broad but heterogeneous, with the highest histotype-level expression in myxofibrosarcoma and undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma. In the patient-linked tissue-microarray cohort, AXL H-score was not associated with metastasis-free or overall survival after clinicopathologic adjustment. ADCT-601 was substantially more potent than a non-targeting anti-gp120 control ADC carrying the same SG3199-containing payload. Free-payload sensitivity varied between cell lines, indicating that intrinsic payload susceptibility contributes to activity, while the payload-matched comparison supports an additional effect of AXL-mediated delivery. ADCT-601 induced cell-cycle perturbation, apoptosis, and γ-H2AX accumulation. Combination experiments identified enhanced activity with DNA damage-response inhibition, particularly ATR inhibition, and in vivo studies supported antitumor activity in two sarcoma xenograft models. These data support biomarker-enriched development of next-generation AXL-directed ADC strategies while emphasizing antigen heterogeneity and therapeutic-index optimization.
